nodes.purpose: Defines the governed product, workflow, and scope boundary for EpistemicOS.
nodes.required_output: BP.1 node set covering product definition, non-scope, workflow, boundaries, category, geography, evidence standards.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: canonical Level 1 domain map, canonical_product_context, internal_architecture; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: BP.1 is used exactly as the fixed Level 1 domain for product, workflow, and scope definition; evidence_rationale: BP.1 is an internal architecture domain, so E1 is sufficient for architecture placement only; cannot_support: demand, adoption, PMF, compliance, feasibility, commercial readiness, or investor readiness.

nodes.linked_uncertainties: linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — BP.1 scope-boundary coherence risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not rename, merge, split, or expand BP.1; must not infer business validity from architecture.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if Level 1 map changes or any BP.1 child conflicts with canonical product context.
nodes.notes_limitations: Parent domain only.

nodes.purpose: Defines the controlled product identity of EpistemicOS without validating demand, adoption, effectiveness, or readiness.
nodes.required_output: Product definition packet covering product identity, unit of analysis, core diagnostic function, diagnostic object, diagnostic output object, human judgment boundary, product state label, and definition acceptance check.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: canonical_product_context, internal_architecture, controller-approved scope charter; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: BP.1.1.1–BP.1.1.8 are present, coherent, and do not contradict the canonical product boundary; evidence_rationale: product definition is an internal architecture boundary that defines what EpistemicOS is; cannot_support: demand, adoption, PMF, diagnostic accuracy, compliance, feasibility, commercial readiness, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Assumes product context current; gap: no signed product-definition packet.
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not claim demand, adoption, PMF, effectiveness, acceptance prediction, or reviewer replacement.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if product positioning, demo, workflow, or output object changes product identity.
nodes.notes_limitations: Architecture only; does not establish demand, adoption, feasibility, or PMF.

nodes.purpose: Define the product in one controlled statement.
nodes.required_output: One-sentence definition of EpistemicOS as a pre-submission academic manuscript diagnostics system.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: canonical_product_context, internal_architecture, controller-approved product wording; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: product identity statement matches the canonical description of EpistemicOS as a pre-submission academic manuscript diagnostics system; evidence_rationale: product identity is a controlled architecture statement, not an external validation claim; cannot_support: demand, adoption, PMF, diagnostic validity, compliance, feasibility, publication improvement, commercial readiness, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: controller-signed wording not attached.
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not claim market demand, PMF, feasibility, diagnostic validity, or publication improvement.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if product description changes in charter, pitch, UI, demo, or business-plan narrative.
nodes.notes_limitations: Must not imply market demand, PMF, adoption, or diagnostic accuracy.

nodes.purpose: Define the unit of analysis that EpistemicOS evaluates and distinguish it from adjacent manuscript, author, reviewer, or publication-outcome objects.
nodes.required_output: Statement that the primary unit of analysis is the atomic manuscript claim, not the manuscript as a general text object.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: canonical_product_context, internal_architecture, claim-ontology specification if available; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: the primary unit of analysis is explicitly defined as the atomic manuscript claim and does not expand into manuscript-level, pricing-unit, transaction-unit, or validation-unit claims; evidence_rationale: unit of analysis is an internal product-architecture boundary; cannot_support: demand, adoption, PMF, pricing validity, validation sufficiency, compliance, feasibility, commercial readiness, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no accepted claim ontology attached.
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not infer pricing, validation unit, or workflow adoption from unit definition.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if primary analytic unit changes from claim-level logic.
nodes.notes_limitations: Must not expand into pricing unit, validation unit, or transaction unit; those route to BP.9/BP.10 where needed.

nodes.purpose: Define the product’s core functional role.
nodes.required_output: Functional statement: makes claim-level weaknesses visible, traceable, and actionable for human academic judgment.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: canonical_product_context, internal_architecture, product-function specification; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: core function is stated as claim-level diagnostic support for human academic judgment and excludes truth determination, acceptance prediction, reviewer replacement, and autonomous decisions; evidence_rationale: functional role can be architecturally defined before performance validation; cannot_support: demand, adoption, PMF, diagnostic accuracy, truth determination, reviewer equivalence, compliance, feasibility, commercial readiness, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no operational performance evidence.
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not claim truth determination, reviewer replacement, acceptance prediction, or autonomous decision-making.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if features, outputs, or positioning imply non-diagnostic or autonomous decision function.
nodes.notes_limitations: Must not claim truth determination, acceptance prediction, or peer-review replacement.

nodes.purpose: Define the artifact or material the system processes.
nodes.required_output: Input-object definition covering manuscript text, claims, evidence, inference, assumptions, contribution, and risk signals.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: canonical_product_context, internal_architecture, product/workflow specification; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: diagnostic input objects are explicitly listed and bounded to manuscript text, claims, evidence, inference, assumptions, contribution, and risk signals; evidence_rationale: diagnostic object definition governs what the product may process within BP.1 scope; cannot_support: demand, adoption, PMF, data-governance compliance, deployability, technical feasibility, diagnostic performance, commercial readiness, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no accepted data schema attached.
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not infer deployability, compliance, feasibility, performance, or adoption.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if input material, object taxonomy, or processing scope changes.
nodes.notes_limitations: Detailed workflow sequencing belongs under BP.1.3, not here.

nodes.purpose: Define the diagnostic output object produced by EpistemicOS and the boundaries of what that output may and may not represent.
nodes.required_output: Output-object definition: diagnostic package with claim-level signals, evidence gaps, inference risks, method-fit risks, uncertainty flags, reviewer-facing concerns, and revision priorities.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: canonical_product_context, internal_architecture, diagnostic-output taxonomy, sample-output audit if examples are used; evidence_tier_required: E1 for architecture; E2/E3 if sample outputs are used as examples; sufficiency_threshold: output object is diagnostic, traceable, bounded, and does not imply publication decision, reviewer score, truth proof, acceptance prediction, or autonomous revision authority; evidence_rationale: output architecture defines what EpistemicOS may produce, while sample-output evidence only supports whether examples follow that boundary; cannot_support: demand, adoption, PMF, diagnostic accuracy, publication improvement, acceptance probability, compliance, feasibility, commercial readiness, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: sample outputs not audited.
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not claim publication decision, acceptance prediction, reviewer score, truth proof, or autonomous revision authority.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if output taxonomy, UI, scoring, or report language implies decision authority or outcome prediction.
nodes.notes_limitations: Output is diagnostic and auditable; it must not be treated as a publication decision, reviewer score, proof of truth, or acceptance prediction.

nodes.purpose: Define the decision boundary between system output and human action.
nodes.required_output: Statement that EpistemicOS supports human academic judgment; humans decide approval, revision, rejection, submission, or escalation.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: canonical_product_context, internal_architecture, workflow specification, decision-authority map; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: human decision boundary is explicit and humans retain approval, revision, rejection, submission, escalation, editorial, and institutional decision authority; evidence_rationale: human judgment role is a governance boundary preventing autonomous-decision overclaiming; cannot_support: demand, adoption, PMF, legal compliance, institutional approval, reviewer equivalence, decision quality, feasibility, commercial readiness, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: deployment permissions model not reviewed.
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not claim autonomous approval, rejection, submission, escalation, editorial decision, or expert replacement.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if output taxonomy, UI, scoring, or report language implies decision authority or outcome prediction.
nodes.notes_limitations: Prevents autonomous-decision overclaiming; connects to BP.1.2 Product Non-Scope.

nodes.purpose: Governs the criteria for assigning a product maturity state without implying readiness, effectiveness, adoption, or validation.
nodes.required_output: Product state criteria set covering concept, prototype, demo, MVP, pilot-ready, deployed, and product-state acceptance check.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: canonical_product_context, internal_architecture, controller-provided product-state artifact; evidence_tier_required: E1 for internal product-state architecture; sufficiency_threshold: BP.1.1.7.1–BP.1.1.7.7 define separate evidence thresholds for each product-state label; evidence_rationale: product maturity labels carry different proof burdens and must not be treated interchangeably; cannot_support: demand, adoption, PMF, compliance, feasibility, commercial readiness, investor readiness, product effectiveness, or technical scalability.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: current product-state data not supplied. Support: dated prototype, demo, MVP, pilot-readiness, or deployment artifact supports the selected state label. Revise: maturity state changes if supplied evidence supports a lower or higher state than claimed. Invalidate: claimed state lacks a supporting artifact or contradicts available product evidence.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — product-state evidence gap; BP.12 candidate — product-state overclaim risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not infer readiness, effectiveness, adoption, PMF, compliance, feasibility, commercial readiness, investor readiness, or deployment validity from a state label.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if product maturity changes, supporting artifact changes, state evidence is contradicted, or product copy overstates readiness.
nodes.notes_limitations: Parent node only. Current state is not populated here.

nodes.purpose: Defines minimum evidence for calling EpistemicOS a concept.
nodes.required_output: Concept-state criteria checklist.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: canonical_product_context, internal_architecture, founder/controller scope artifact; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: there is a controller-approved concept description defining product identity, intended user/workflow, diagnostic purpose, and non-scope boundary; evidence_rationale: concept state is an internal planning label supported by scope and architecture artifacts; cannot_support: demand, adoption, PMF, compliance, feasibility, commercial readiness, investor readiness, prototype existence, demo readiness, MVP readiness, pilot readiness, or deployment.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no controller-approved concept artifact supplied. Support: signed concept note or scope charter. Revise: artifact shows product has progressed beyond concept. Invalidate: no coherent product concept exists or concept contradicts BP.1.1/BP.1.2.
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not claim the concept is built, usable, validated, demo-ready, pilot-ready, deployed, feasible, wanted, or commercially ready.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if product identity, scope, non-scope, or concept artifact changes.
nodes.notes_limitations: Lowest maturity label. Supports architecture description only.

nodes.purpose: Defines minimum evidence for calling EpistemicOS a prototype.

nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if prototype artifact changes, core diagnostic function changes, or prototype is represented as MVP/pilot-ready without evidence.
nodes.notes_limitations: Prototype evidence shows existence of a working artifact only, not effectiveness.

nodes.purpose: Defines minimum evidence for calling EpistemicOS demo-ready.

nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not claim demo readiness proves usability, buyer interest, technical feasibility, product completeness, pilot readiness, deployment readiness, or commercial readiness.

Revise: artifact supports only demo/prototype or supports pilot-ready. Invalidate: product cannot complete the minimum diagnostic workflow or violates non-scope boundaries.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — MVP-state artifact gap; BP.12 candidate — MVP-readiness overclaim risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not claim MVP status proves adoption, product effectiveness, diagnostic validity, market demand, technical scalability, compliance readiness, pilot readiness, or commercial readiness.

nodes.node_title: Evidence Mapping and Inference Checking Architecture
nodes.purpose: Define how EpistemicOS maps claims to supporting evidence and checks for inference errors, method–claim fit issues, and citation–claim support gaps, without asserting checking accuracy.

nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: inference check types or mapping logic not specified. Support: technical specification reviewed by academic expert advisor. nodes.node_title: Core Problem, Urgency, and Governing Hypothesis
nodes.purpose: Governs the core problem definition, pain and consequence architecture, urgency and priority hypothesis, why-now hypothesis, governing hypothesis architecture, evidence standards, and branch acceptance gate without asserting demand, urgency, buyer intent, PMF, or commercial readiness.
nodes.required_output: BP.2 Level 2 node set: BP.2.1 Core Problem Definition; BP.2.2 Pain and Consequence Architecture; BP.2.3 Urgency and Priority Hypothesis; BP.2.4 Why-Now Hypothesis; BP.2.5 Governing Hypothesis Architecture; BP.2.6 Problem-to-Claim Evidence Standards; BP.2.7 Acceptance and Reopen Gate.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: canonical_product_context, internal_architecture, founder hypothesis, customer-discovery evidence where governed, BP.3-governed external sources; evidence_tier_required: E1 for problem architecture, E4+ for discovery evidence supporting problem claims; sufficiency_threshold: all BP.2 sections are populated, coherent, and internally consistent without asserting demand, WTP, or adoption; evidence_rationale: problem architecture is hypothetical until evidenced through BP.6 discovery and BP.10 validation; cannot_support: demand, adoption, WTP, PMF, procurement readiness, commercial readiness, or investor readiness.

Revise: if BP.1 scope, product definition, or discovery evidence changes any problem claim. Invalidate: if problem cannot be stated in falsifiable, bounded terms.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — BP.2 architecture-incompleteness risk; BP.12 candidate — problem-definition overclaim risk; BP.12 candidate — governing-hypothesis uncertainty
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not infer demand, adoption, urgency, WTP, procurement readiness, PMF, commercial readiness, or investor readiness from problem architecture. Must not treat problem definition as market validation.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if BP.1 product scope changes, discovery evidence contradicts problem architecture, BP.6 reveals different user jobs or pain, BP.10 validation falsifies the governing hypothesis, or any BP.2 child section changes.
nodes.notes_limitations: BP.2 is the problem and hypothesis architecture domain; it does not validate the problem. Validation routes to BP.6 (discovery) and BP.10 (pilot/PMF evidence). The governing hypothesis in BP.2.5 is a test object, not a conclusion.

nodes.purpose: Defines the governed problem claim without validating demand, severity, or market size.
nodes.required_output: Problem statement; affected workflow context; claimant/user distinction; problem-boundary exclusions; problem-definition acceptance check.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: founder scope input, customer-discovery evidence where external claims are made, BP.3-governed sources; evidence_tier_required: E1 for candidate architecture, E4+ for user-reported problem claims, E6+ for institutional problem claims; sufficiency_threshold: problem is stated as a falsifiable candidate claim and separated from evidence of adoption, WTP, procurement readiness, or PMF; evidence_rationale: problem definition frames what must be tested; cannot_support: demand, willingness to pay, procurement readiness, adoption, PMF, market size, commercial urgency, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Assumes the problem can be defined without validating it. Gap: no governed external problem evidence populated. Support: coded discovery evidence or institution-level evidence. Revise if users, buyers, or institutions define the problem differently.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — problem-definition uncertainty; BP.12 candidate — problem-scope ambiguity
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not claim the problem is widespread, urgent, severe, validated, monetisable, procurement-backed, or institutionally accepted without required evidence.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if BP.1 product/workflow scope changes, discovery evidence contradicts the problem definition, or BP.6 shows users frame the problem differently.
nodes.notes_limitations: Defines the problem architecture only; validation routes to BP.6 and BP.10.

nodes.purpose: State the governed problem claim in one falsifiable, bounded sentence without implying validation, demand, or urgency.
nodes.required_output: One-sentence problem statement identifying the governed pain, the affected actor, the workflow context, and the observable gap — without PMF, urgency, or severity inference.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: canonical_product_context, founder hypothesis, customer-discovery evidence where external claims are made, BP.3-governed sources; evidence_tier_required: E1 for candidate problem statement, E4+ for user-validated problem evidence, E6+ for institutional problem validation; sufficiency_threshold: problem is stated as a falsifiable candidate claim bounded to a specific actor, workflow, and observable gap; evidence_rationale: problem statement frames what must be tested and governs downstream pain, urgency, and hypothesis architecture; cannot_support: demand, WTP, procurement readiness, adoption, PMF, market size, commercial urgency, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: controller-approved problem wording not attached. Support: coded discovery interviews confirming the problem as described. Revise: if users frame the problem differently or discovery shows a different root cause. Invalidate: if no evidence of the problem gap can be surfaced in user or institutional context.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — problem-statement falsifiability; BP.12 candidate — problem-wording overclaim risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not claim the problem is widespread, severe, urgent, validated, monetisable, or procurement-backed. Must not conflate problem existence with problem relevance or buyer priority.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if product/workflow scope changes, discovery evidence contradicts the problem framing, or BP.6 shows users define the problem differently.
nodes.notes_limitations: Problem statement is the anchor for all downstream BP.2 child nodes; any change to wording requires re-audit of BP.2.1.2–BP.2.1.9.

nodes.purpose: Define what the governed problem does and does not include, preventing scope inflation and overclaiming.
nodes.required_output: Problem inclusion/exclusion register: what conditions, actors, workflows, and manifestations are inside and outside the governed problem boundary.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: canonical_product_context, internal_architecture, BP.1.2 non-scope, founder hypothesis; evidence_tier_required: E1 for architecture; sufficiency_threshold: inclusions and exclusions are explicit, non-overlapping, and consistent with BP.1 product/workflow scope; evidence_rationale: boundary prevents downstream problem inflation and prohibited inference; cannot_support: demand, urgency, PMF, severity, or adoption.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: boundary register not formalised. Support: accepted product-context and workflow map. Revise: if problem framing expands or contracts through discovery. Invalidate: if boundary conflicts with BP.1.2 non-scope exclusions.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — problem boundary ambiguity; BP.12 candidate — scope-inflation risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not infer urgency, severity, or demand from boundary definition. Must not treat boundary completeness as problem validation.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if BP.1 scope changes, discovery expands or narrows the problem, or downstream BP nodes create boundary conflicts.
nodes.notes_limitations: Boundary register is prerequisite for non-scope exclusion audit in BP.1.2 cross-check.

nodes.purpose: Identify the specific workflow stage, user task, or decision moment where the governed problem is hypothesised to occur.
nodes.required_output: Workflow-problem mapping: problem location in BP.1.3 task sequence; before/after state description; human decision points impacted.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: canonical_product_context, BP.1.3 workflow architecture, workflow evidence; evidence_tier_required: E1 for workflow-location mapping, E4+ for user-confirmed workflow disruption, E6+ for institutional workflow evidence; sufficiency_threshold: problem is traceable to at least one specific workflow task or decision point without implying adoption; evidence_rationale: workflow location governs diagnostic scope and distinguishes intended use from unsupported extrapolation; cannot_support: adoption, urgency, WTP, procurement readiness, or institutional workflow change.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no user-validated workflow disruption evidence. Support: discovery interviews, workflow observation, institutional workflow logs. Revise: if users perform workflow differently or problem manifests at different stage. Invalidate: if no workflow stage can be linked to the problem.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — workflow-problem location uncertainty; BP.12 candidate — workflow-adoption inference risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not infer adoption, repeated use, or institutional acceptance from workflow-problem mapping.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if BP.1.3 workflow map changes, discovery shows problem at different task, or pilot evidence locates problem differently.
nodes.notes_limitations: Workflow mapping must reference BP.1.3 task sequence; changes to BP.1.3 automatically reopen this node.

nodes.purpose: Identify which stakeholders are hypothesised to experience the governed problem, distinguishing claimants from buyers and users.
nodes.required_output: Stakeholder problem map: stakeholder type, relationship to problem, distinction between problem-experiencer (user), problem-acknowledger (buyer), and problem-denier; severity hypothesis per stakeholder.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: canonical_product_context, BP.5 stakeholder architecture, founder hypothesis; evidence_tier_required: E1 for stakeholder identification, E4+ for user-confirmed problem experience, E6+ for institutional stakeholder validation; sufficiency_threshold: stakeholder types are distinct, linked to problem manifestation, and not conflated with buyers, funders, or institutional decision-makers; evidence_rationale: stakeholder distinction prevents audience conflation and demand inference; cannot_support: WTP, procurement intent, budget approval, adoption, PMF, or institutional demand.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no discovery evidence per stakeholder type. Support: coded interviews per stakeholder type. Revise: if new stakeholder types emerge or problem affects different actors. Invalidate: if primary problem-experiencer is misidentified.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — stakeholder-type clarity; BP.12 candidate — claimant-buyer conflation risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not conflate problem-experiencer with budget-holder or procurement authority. Must not infer WTP or adoption from problem acknowledgement.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if BP.5 stakeholder architecture changes, discovery reveals different affected populations, or buyer/user distinction is contradicted.
nodes.notes_limitations: Stakeholder mapping is distinct from BP.5 role map; BP.2.1.4 governs who experiences the problem, BP.5 governs who buys.

nodes.purpose: Define the observable, describable ways the governed problem appears in the affected workflow without asserting frequency or severity.
nodes.required_output: Manifestation register: observable signals, failure modes, workaround behaviours, friction points, and consequence indicators hypothesised to accompany the problem.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: founder hypothesis, customer-discovery evidence, workflow observation; evidence_tier_required: E1 for candidate manifestation list, E4+ for user-confirmed manifestations, E6+ for institutional manifestation evidence; sufficiency_threshold: manifestations are observable, bounded to the governed workflow, and not inferred from product assumptions; evidence_rationale: manifestation definition anchors what discovery and pilot evidence must confirm; cannot_support: frequency, prevalence, severity, demand, WTP, or PMF.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no discovery evidence confirming manifestations as described. Support: coded user interviews, workflow observation, incident logs. Revise: if users report different failure modes or workarounds. Invalidate: if no observable manifestation can be surfaced.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — manifestation-evidence gap; BP.12 candidate — manifestation-overclaim risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not infer frequency, severity, or urgency from manifestation description. Must not claim manifestations are universal or representative.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if discovery reveals different manifestation patterns, problem is not observable in the workflow, or pilot evidence contradicts manifestation register.
nodes.notes_limitations: Manifestation evidence is the first point at which discovery interviews become citable; requires BP.3.7 coding governance.

nodes.purpose: State all assumptions underpinning the problem definition that are not yet evidenced, including actor, workflow, frequency, and severity assumptions.
nodes.required_output: Assumption register: each assumption stated explicitly, linked to the problem component it supports, labelled as unvalidated, with falsification condition and support/revise/invalidate triggers.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: internal architecture, founder hypothesis, assumption ledger; evidence_tier_required: E1 for candidate assumption register, E4+ for assumption-validation evidence; sufficiency_threshold: all major problem assumptions are explicit, labelled as unvalidated, and linked to falsification conditions; evidence_rationale: assumption governance prevents hidden overclaiming; cannot_support: assumption validity, problem severity, demand, urgency, or PMF.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: assumption register not formalised. Support: completed assumption ledger with falsification conditions. Revise: if discovery validates or contradicts assumptions. Invalidate: if assumptions are unstated or non-falsifiable.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — assumption completeness; BP.12 candidate — hidden-assumption risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat assumption completeness as validation. Must not present assumptions as facts.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if discovery evidence validates, revises, or invalidates any assumption, or if new assumptions are identified.
nodes.notes_limitations: Assumption register feeds directly into BP.12; all assumptions must carry explicit falsification conditions.

nodes.purpose: Define the evidence type, tier, source family, and sufficiency threshold required before strengthening the problem claim beyond candidate status.
nodes.required_output: Evidence requirements matrix: evidence tier per claim type, permitted source families, sufficiency thresholds, and escalation routes to BP.3, BP.6, and BP.12.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: Architecture Governance Rules, Evidence Ladder, BP.3 source governance; evidence_tier_required: E1 for evidence-requirement architecture; sufficiency_threshold: each problem sub-claim has a documented evidence tier, source family, and sufficiency threshold; evidence_rationale: evidence requirements define proof burden before claim strengthening; cannot_support: problem validation, demand, PMF, urgency, or commercial traction.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no evidence-requirements matrix. Support: completed matrix aligned with Evidence Ladder and BP.3. Revise: if Evidence Ladder thresholds change. Invalidate: if requirements conflict with BP.3 source governance.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — evidence-requirement completeness; BP.12 candidate — insufficient-tier risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat evidence requirements as evidence itself. Must not infer validation from governance.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if Evidence Ladder changes, BP.3 source governance shifts, or problem claim types expand.
nodes.notes_limitations: Evidence requirements are defined here and enforced in BP.2.6; no duplication of BP.3 source governance.

nodes.purpose: Define all conclusions that BP.2.1 problem evidence must never support, regardless of evidence quantity or source quality.
nodes.required_output: Prohibited-claims register: each prohibited claim explicitly stated, linked to the problem component it protects, with escalation trigger if violated.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: Architecture Governance Rules, BP.1.2 non-scope, BP.2.6 evidence standards; evidence_tier_required: E1 for prohibited-claims architecture; sufficiency_threshold: all prohibited inference patterns are explicitly documented and exhaustive; evidence_rationale: prohibitions protect problem architecture from urgency, demand, and adoption overclaiming; cannot_support: demand, WTP, procurement readiness, PMF, adoption, institutional acceptance, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: prohibition register not populated. Support: completed prohibition matrix aligned with BP.1.2 and BP.2.6. Revise: if new prohibited patterns emerge. Invalidate: if prohibitions are internally contradictory or incomplete.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — prohibited-claim completeness; BP.12 candidate — implicit-overclaim risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not allow any prohibited claim regardless of supporting evidence. Must not treat absence of prohibition as permission.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if BP.1.2 non-scope changes, new inference patterns emerge, or downstream narrative implies prohibited claims.

nodes.purpose: Confirm that BP.2.1 is internally coherent, complete, and free of prohibited claims before downstream pain, urgency, and hypothesis architecture proceeds.

nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: completed BP.2.1.1–BP.2.1.8, architecture audit, controller review; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: BP.2.1.1–BP.2.1.8 are complete, coherent, non-contradictory, and free of prohibited claims; evidence_rationale: acceptance check verifies architecture coherence only; cannot_support: problem validity, demand, severity, urgency, PMF, compliance, feasibility, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: controller approval not recorded. Support: completed architecture review with no contradictions. Revise: if any BP.2.1 child changes. Invalidate: if contradictions or unresolved prohibited claims remain.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — problem-definition acceptance gap; BP.12 candidate — architecture-coherence risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat architecture acceptance as problem validation, severity confirmation, demand evidence, or investor readiness.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if any BP.2.1 child changes, BP.1 scope changes, or discovery evidence contradicts the governed problem definition.
nodes.notes_limitations: Architecture-only gate; acceptance here does not imply problem validation, severity confirmation, or demand evidence.

nodes.purpose: Defines what pain, friction, cost, risk, or consequence the problem is hypothesised to create.
nodes.required_output: Pain taxonomy; consequence map; affected stakeholder table; consequence-evidence requirements; severity-boundary rules.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: founder hypothesis, user interviews, institutional evidence, BP.3-governed sources; evidence_tier_required: E1 for pain taxonomy, E4+ for user pain evidence, E6+ for institutional consequence evidence; sufficiency_threshold: pain and consequence claims are separated by stakeholder type and evidence tier; evidence_rationale: pain architecture prevents unsupported urgency and demand inference; cannot_support: WTP, budget availability, procurement readiness, PMF, adoption, or commercial traction.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Assumes pain and consequence are unvalidated until evidenced. Gap: no coded pain or consequence evidence populated. Support: user discovery, institutional documents, workflow logs, or pilot evidence. Revise if pain is weaker, differently located, or not linked to the proposed workflow.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — pain-evidence gap; BP.12 candidate — consequence-overclaim risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not infer willingness to pay, procurement readiness, adoption intent, institutional urgency, or demand from pain alone.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if discovery shows different pain sources, weaker pain, different consequences, or stakeholder mismatch.
nodes.notes_limitations: Pain is not demand; consequence is not willingness to pay.

nodes.purpose: Define and classify the types of pain hypothesised to result from the governed problem by affected stakeholder and workflow stage.
nodes.required_output: Pain taxonomy: pain type label, description, affected stakeholder, workflow stage, pain mechanism, and evidence-tier required per type.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: founder hypothesis, customer-discovery evidence, workflow observation, BP.3-governed sources; evidence_tier_required: E1 for pain taxonomy, E4+ for user-reported pain evidence, E6+ for institutional pain evidence; sufficiency_threshold: pain types are classified by mechanism (cognitive, operational, reputational, financial, temporal), stakeholder, and workflow stage without conflating pain existence with demand; evidence_rationale: pain taxonomy establishes what must be confirmed in discovery and pilot; cannot_support: WTP, urgency, procurement readiness, adoption, PMF, or commercial traction.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no coded discovery evidence per pain type. Support: coded user interviews per pain mechanism. Revise: if users identify different pain types or mechanisms. Invalidate: if no pain can be confirmed as linked to the governed problem.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — pain-type evidence gap; BP.12 candidate — pain-type overclaim risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not infer WTP, urgency, or procurement readiness from pain type identification. Must not claim pain is universal or representative.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if discovery reveals different pain types, pain mechanism changes, or pain is located at a different workflow stage.
nodes.notes_limitations: Pain taxonomy feeds BP.6 discovery design; changes to pain types require re-coding of existing interview evidence.

nodes.purpose: Define the categories of downstream consequences hypothesised to result from unresolved pain across stakeholder types.
nodes.required_output: Consequence register: consequence category, affected stakeholder, consequence mechanism, consequence time-horizon (immediate/deferred/cumulative), and evidence required.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: founder hypothesis, customer-discovery evidence, institutional documents, BP.3-governed sources; evidence_tier_required: E1 for consequence taxonomy, E4+ for user-confirmed consequence evidence, E6+ for institutional consequence evidence; sufficiency_threshold: consequence categories are classified by type (reputational, epistemic, productivity, career, institutional), linked to pain types, and not conflated with WTP or demand; evidence_rationale: consequence architecture anchors what severity and urgency claims must be tested against; cannot_support: WTP, procurement readiness, urgency, adoption, PMF, or commercial traction.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no discovery evidence per consequence category. Support: coded interviews and institutional documents confirming consequences. Revise: if consequences are weaker, slower, or differently distributed than hypothesised. Invalidate: if consequences are not traceable to the governed problem.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — consequence-evidence gap; BP.12 candidate — consequence-overclaim risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not infer urgency, WTP, or institutional demand from consequence description. Must not claim consequences are inevitable or universal.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if discovery reveals different consequences, consequence time-horizon is misspecified, or consequence evidence is weaker than hypothesised.
nodes.notes_limitations: Consequence categories must be distinguished from pain types; consequence is downstream impact, pain is immediate disruption.

nodes.purpose: Map each governed pain type and consequence to a specific stakeholder type, distinguishing primary experiencer from secondary and institutional actors.
nodes.required_output: Stakeholder-pain matrix: stakeholder type × pain type × consequence category × evidence tier required.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: BP.5 stakeholder architecture, customer-discovery evidence, BP.3-governed sources; evidence_tier_required: E1 for mapping architecture, E4+ for stakeholder-specific pain evidence; sufficiency_threshold: mapping is unambiguous, stakeholder types are not conflated, and no pain or consequence is assigned without linking to a specific actor; evidence_rationale: stakeholder-pain mapping prevents audience conflation and unsupported generalisation; cannot_support: WTP per stakeholder, procurement authority, adoption intent, or institutional demand.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no per-stakeholder pain evidence. Support: coded discovery evidence per stakeholder type. Revise: if pain distribution shifts across stakeholder types. Invalidate: if primary experiencer is misidentified.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — stakeholder-pain mapping ambiguity; BP.12 candidate — audience-conflation risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not conflate pain-experiencer with budget-holder. Must not infer WTP or adoption intent from pain acknowledgement by any stakeholder type.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if BP.5 stakeholder architecture changes, discovery reveals different stakeholder pain distribution, or buyer/user distinction is contradicted.
nodes.notes_limitations: Stakeholder-pain matrix must remain consistent with BP.2.1.4 and BP.5; conflation of pain-experiencer with budget-holder is the primary overclaim risk here.

nodes.purpose: Define severity levels for governed pain types and consequences using an explicit, evidence-gated classification scale.
nodes.required_output: Severity classification scale: severity levels defined (trivial/moderate/significant/critical), assignment criteria, evidence required per level, and prohibited severity upgrades without evidence.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: customer-discovery evidence, workflow observation, institutional documents, BP.3-governed sources; evidence_tier_required: E1 for severity classification architecture, E4+ for user-confirmed severity, E6+ for institutional severity evidence; sufficiency_threshold: severity levels are explicitly defined with evidence thresholds; no severity upgrade may occur without meeting the corresponding evidence tier; evidence_rationale: severity classification prevents unsupported urgency and demand inference; cannot_support: WTP, procurement readiness, urgency, adoption, PMF, or commercial traction.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no discovery evidence per severity level. Support: coded discovery evidence with explicit severity signals. Revise: if users rate severity differently or consequences are less disruptive than hypothesised. Invalidate: if no differential severity signal can be surfaced.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — severity-classification evidence gap; BP.12 candidate — severity-escalation risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not infer urgency, WTP, or procurement readiness from severity classification. Must not upgrade severity without meeting required evidence tier.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if discovery evidence supports different severity levels, consequence evidence weakens, or pilot evidence contradicts severity classification.
nodes.notes_limitations: Severity classification must not be used to imply urgency; severity and urgency are governed separately in BP.2.2 and BP.2.3.

nodes.purpose: State all unvalidated assumptions underpinning the pain and consequence architecture, labelled explicitly as unvalidated with falsification conditions.
nodes.required_output: Pain assumption register: each assumption, the pain/consequence component it supports, labelled as unvalidated, with support/revise/invalidate evidence triggers.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: internal architecture, founder hypothesis, assumption ledger; evidence_tier_required: E1 for candidate assumption register, E4+ for assumption-validation evidence; sufficiency_threshold: all pain and consequence assumptions are explicit, labelled as unvalidated, and falsifiable; evidence_rationale: assumption governance prevents hidden overclaiming in pain and consequence architecture; cannot_support: pain validity, consequence severity, demand, urgency, or PMF.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: assumption register not formalised. Support: completed assumption ledger with falsification conditions. Revise: if discovery validates or contradicts assumptions. Invalidate: if assumptions are unstated or non-falsifiable.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — pain-assumption completeness; BP.12 candidate — hidden-pain-assumption risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat assumption completeness as pain validation. Must not present pain assumptions as facts or confirmed observations.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if discovery validates, revises, or invalidates any pain assumption, or new assumptions are identified.
nodes.notes_limitations: All pain assumptions feed BP.12; completeness review required before pain claims are used in GTM or investor narrative.

nodes.purpose: Identify the upstream conditions, stakeholder behaviours, and workflow factors that must be present for each consequence to materialise.
nodes.required_output: Consequence dependency map: consequence category × prerequisite condition × dependency type (necessary/sufficient/probabilistic) × evidence required.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: internal architecture, founder hypothesis, discovery evidence; evidence_tier_required: E1 for dependency architecture, E4+ for evidence of dependency conditions; sufficiency_threshold: all consequence dependencies are explicit and non-circular; evidence_rationale: dependency mapping prevents consequence claims that outrun their conditions; cannot_support: consequence inevitability, severity, urgency, WTP, or PMF.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: dependency map not formalised. Support: discovery and workflow evidence confirming dependency conditions. Revise: if dependency conditions are missing or different. Invalidate: if dependencies are circular or unfalsifiable.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — consequence-dependency clarity; BP.12 candidate — false-necessity risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not claim consequences are inevitable, universal, or independent of conditions. Must not treat dependency completeness as consequence validation.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if discovery shows different dependency conditions, workflow changes alter consequence pathways, or pilot evidence contradicts dependency assumptions.
nodes.notes_limitations: Consequence dependency map governs which pain-consequence chains are conditional vs unconditional; unconditional claims are prohibited.

nodes.purpose: Define the evidence type, tier, source family, and sufficiency threshold required before strengthening pain or consequence claims beyond candidate status.
nodes.required_output: Pain evidence requirements matrix: evidence tier per pain/consequence claim type, permitted source families, sufficiency thresholds, escalation routes to BP.3, BP.6, and BP.12.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: Architecture Governance Rules, Evidence Ladder, BP.3 source governance; evidence_tier_required: E1 for evidence-requirement architecture; sufficiency_threshold: each pain and consequence claim type has documented evidence tier, source family, and sufficiency threshold; evidence_rationale: evidence requirements define proof burden before claim strengthening; cannot_support: pain validation, consequence confirmation, demand, PMF, or commercial traction.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no evidence-requirements matrix. Support: completed matrix aligned with Evidence Ladder and BP.3. Revise: if Evidence Ladder thresholds change. Invalidate: if requirements conflict with BP.3 source governance.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — pain-evidence-requirement completeness; BP.12 candidate — insufficient-tier risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat evidence requirements as evidence itself. Must not infer validation from governance.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if Evidence Ladder changes, BP.3 source governance shifts, or pain claim types expand.
nodes.notes_limitations: Evidence requirements defined here feed BP.2.6.2; must be consistent with Evidence Ladder and BP.3.7 discovery governance.

nodes.purpose: Define all conclusions that BP.2.2 pain and consequence evidence must never support, regardless of evidence quantity.
nodes.required_output: Prohibited-inference register for pain: each prohibited conclusion, pain/consequence component it protects, and escalation trigger if violated.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: Architecture Governance Rules, BP.1.2 non-scope, BP.2.6 evidence standards; evidence_tier_required: E1 for prohibited-inference architecture; sufficiency_threshold: all prohibited pain inferences are explicitly documented and exhaustive; evidence_rationale: prohibitions protect pain architecture from urgency, demand, and adoption overclaiming; cannot_support: WTP, procurement readiness, urgency, adoption, PMF, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: prohibition register not populated. Support: completed prohibition matrix. Revise: if new prohibited patterns emerge. Invalidate: if prohibitions are internally contradictory.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — prohibited-pain-inference completeness; BP.12 candidate — implicit-overclaim risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not allow any prohibited inference regardless of pain evidence strength. Must not treat absence of prohibition as permission.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if BP.2.6 evidence standards change, new inference patterns emerge, or downstream narrative implies prohibited pain claims.
nodes.notes_limitations: Prohibited inference register is the primary overclaim-prevention mechanism for pain architecture; any downstream use of pain evidence must pass this gate.

nodes.purpose: Confirm that BP.2.2 is internally coherent, complete, and free of prohibited inferences before downstream urgency and hypothesis architecture proceeds.
nodes.required_output: Acceptance checklist: pain types, consequence categories, stakeholder-pain map, severity classification, assumptions, consequence dependencies, evidence requirements, and prohibited inferences are present, coherent, and non-contradictory.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: completed BP.2.2.1–BP.2.2.8, architecture audit, controller review; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: BP.2.2.1–BP.2.2.8 are complete, coherent, non-contradictory, and free of prohibited inferences; evidence_rationale: acceptance check verifies architecture coherence only; cannot_support: pain validity, consequence confirmation, demand, urgency, PMF, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: controller approval not recorded. Support: completed architecture review. Revise: if any BP.2.2 child changes. Invalidate: if contradictions remain.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — pain-acceptance gap; BP.12 candidate — architecture-coherence risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat pain-architecture acceptance as pain validation, consequence confirmation, severity evidence, or demand proof.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if any BP.2.2 child changes, discovery evidence contradicts pain architecture, or BP.6 reveals different pain distribution.
nodes.notes_limitations: Architecture-only gate; pain evidence is still hypothesis until BP.6 discovery and BP.10 pilot evidence are populated.

nodes.purpose: Defines whether the problem is hypothesised to be urgent, time-sensitive, or decision-relevant for users, buyers, or institutions.
nodes.required_output: Urgency hypothesis; priority criteria; timing triggers; urgency-evidence threshold; urgency acceptance check.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: user discovery, buyer discovery, institutional evidence, workflow evidence; evidence_tier_required: E1 for candidate urgency logic, E4+ for user-priority evidence, E6+ for institutional priority or budget-cycle relevance; sufficiency_threshold: urgency is stated as a testable hypothesis and not inferred from pain or category interest; evidence_rationale: urgency must be independently evidenced before supporting prioritisation; cannot_support: procurement readiness, budget approval, adoption, purchase intent, PMF, or commercial traction.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Assumes urgency is distinct from pain intensity. Gap: no priority or timing evidence populated. Support: discovery evidence showing current prioritisation or institutional timing triggers. Revise if the problem is real but not urgent.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — urgency-validation gap; BP.12 candidate — priority-mismatch risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not claim “urgent,” “must-have,” “priority,” “budgeted,” or “decision-critical” without direct priority evidence.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if users acknowledge the problem but do not prioritise it, or if buyer/institutional timing evidence contradicts urgency.
nodes.notes_limitations: Urgency requires separate evidence from pain.

nodes.purpose: State what urgency means in the context of the governed problem: the conditions under which a stakeholder would prioritise resolving it now rather than later.
nodes.required_output: Urgency definition statement: urgency criteria, timeframe logic, trigger conditions, and distinction from pain severity.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: founder hypothesis, customer-discovery evidence, BP.3-governed sources; evidence_tier_required: E1 for urgency definition, E4+ for user-confirmed urgency evidence, E6+ for institutional urgency evidence; sufficiency_threshold: urgency is defined separately from pain severity and linked to observable timing conditions or prioritisation signals; evidence_rationale: urgency definition establishes what must be tested in discovery; cannot_support: demand, WTP, procurement readiness, adoption, PMF, or budget availability.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no discovery evidence confirming urgency conditions as defined. Support: coded discovery interviews with explicit timing or prioritisation signals. Revise: if users acknowledge pain but do not prioritise resolution. Invalidate: if no urgency signal can be surfaced.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — urgency-definition evidence gap; BP.12 candidate — pain-urgency conflation risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not infer urgency from pain severity. Must not claim urgency without direct priority evidence. Must not conflate "important" with "urgent".
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if discovery shows urgency conditions differ from definition, or urgency is absent even when pain is confirmed.
nodes.notes_limitations: Urgency definition must be operationalised before it can be tested in BP.10 pilot; a non-operationalised urgency claim cannot be falsified.

nodes.purpose: Define the criteria by which the governed problem would be ranked above competing priorities by each affected stakeholder type.
nodes.required_output: Priority criteria matrix: stakeholder type × competing priority × criteria for outranking × evidence tier required.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: customer-discovery evidence, buyer discovery evidence, BP.5 stakeholder architecture, BP.3-governed sources; evidence_tier_required: E1 for priority criteria architecture, E4+ for user priority evidence, E6+ for institutional priority evidence; sufficiency_threshold: priority criteria are specific, stakeholder-differentiated, and explicitly contrast the governed problem with competing priorities; evidence_rationale: priority criteria prevent unsupported demand and WTP inference; cannot_support: WTP, budget approval, adoption, PMF, or procurement readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no per-stakeholder priority evidence. Support: coded discovery with explicit priority trade-off signals. Revise: if problem ranks lower than competing priorities. Invalidate: if problem is consistently deprioritised.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — priority-criteria evidence gap; BP.12 candidate — priority-mismatch risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not infer WTP or procurement readiness from priority criteria definition. Must not claim the problem outranks competing priorities without evidence.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if discovery evidence shows problem is deprioritised, stakeholder priorities shift, or institutional budget constraints change.
nodes.notes_limitations: Priority criteria differ by stakeholder type; generalising priority across stakeholders is a prohibited inference.

nodes.purpose: Identify the events, deadlines, or conditions that would create a timing-sensitive window during which the governed problem demands resolution.
nodes.required_output: Timing trigger register: trigger event, affected stakeholder, urgency window, frequency hypothesis, and evidence required.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: founder hypothesis, customer-discovery evidence, workflow observation, BP.3-governed sources; evidence_tier_required: E1 for trigger identification, E4+ for user-confirmed timing triggers, E6+ for institutional deadline evidence; sufficiency_threshold: timing triggers are specific, linked to stakeholder workflow, and not inferred from product assumptions or market trends; evidence_rationale: timing triggers ground urgency in observable events rather than assumptions; cannot_support: demand frequency, WTP, procurement readiness, or PMF.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no discovery evidence confirming timing triggers. Support: coded discovery with explicit timing or deadline signals. Revise: if timing triggers are absent or weaker than hypothesised. Invalidate: if no timing trigger can be identified in user context.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — timing-trigger evidence gap; BP.12 candidate — false-timing-urgency risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not infer demand frequency or procurement urgency from timing trigger identification. Must not treat trigger existence as demand evidence.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if discovery reveals different timing patterns, institutional calendar changes, or workflow redesign removes timing triggers.
nodes.notes_limitations: Timing triggers feed BP.5.5 budget cycle and BP.9.3.4 GTM sequencing; inconsistency between BP.2.3.3 and BP.5.5 requires reopen.

nodes.purpose: Map urgency and timing trigger evidence to each stakeholder type, distinguishing between who experiences urgency and who controls resolution priority.
nodes.required_output: Stakeholder-urgency matrix: stakeholder type × urgency signal × timing trigger × resolution authority × evidence tier required.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: BP.5 stakeholder architecture, customer-discovery evidence, BP.3-governed sources; evidence_tier_required: E1 for mapping architecture, E4+ for stakeholder-specific urgency evidence; sufficiency_threshold: urgency is mapped separately by stakeholder type and resolution authority is distinguished from pain-experiencer; evidence_rationale: stakeholder-urgency mapping prevents conflation of pain with institutional decision-making authority; cannot_support: WTP per stakeholder, procurement authority, budget approval, or adoption intent.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no per-stakeholder urgency mapping evidence. Support: coded discovery per stakeholder. Revise: if resolution authority rests with a different stakeholder than the pain-experiencer. Invalidate: if no stakeholder with resolution authority assigns priority.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — stakeholder-urgency mapping ambiguity; BP.12 candidate — authority-conflation risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not conflate urgency-experiencer with decision-maker or budget-holder. Must not infer procurement readiness from stakeholder priority mapping.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if BP.5 stakeholder architecture changes, resolution authority is reassigned, or urgency mapping is contradicted by discovery.
nodes.notes_limitations: Stakeholder-urgency matrix must not conflate urgency-experiencer with budget-holder; cross-reference to BP.5.2 buying centre required.

nodes.purpose: State all unvalidated assumptions underpinning the urgency and priority hypothesis, labelled as unvalidated with falsification conditions.
nodes.required_output: Urgency assumption register: each assumption, urgency component supported, labelled as unvalidated, with support/revise/invalidate triggers.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: internal architecture, founder hypothesis, assumption ledger; evidence_tier_required: E1 for candidate assumption register, E4+ for validation evidence; sufficiency_threshold: all urgency assumptions are explicit, labelled as unvalidated, and falsifiable; evidence_rationale: assumption governance prevents hidden urgency overclaiming; cannot_support: urgency validity, prioritisation evidence, demand, or PMF.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: assumption register not formalised. Support: completed assumption ledger with falsification conditions. Revise: if discovery validates or contradicts assumptions. Invalidate: if assumptions are unstated.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — urgency-assumption completeness; BP.12 candidate — hidden-urgency-assumption risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat urgency assumption completeness as urgency validation.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if discovery validates, revises, or invalidates any urgency assumption.
nodes.notes_limitations: All urgency assumptions feed BP.12; urgency is among the most commonly inflated early-stage claims.

nodes.purpose: Identify the upstream conditions and stakeholder behaviours that must be present for urgency to materialise.
nodes.required_output: Urgency dependency map: urgency condition × prerequisite factor × dependency type × evidence required.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: internal architecture, founder hypothesis, discovery evidence; evidence_tier_required: E1 for dependency architecture, E4+ for dependency condition evidence; sufficiency_threshold: all urgency dependencies are explicit and non-circular; evidence_rationale: dependency mapping prevents urgency claims that outrun their conditions; cannot_support: urgency inevitability, severity, procurement readiness, or PMF.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: dependency map not formalised. Support: discovery evidence confirming dependency conditions. Revise: if dependency conditions are missing. Invalidate: if dependencies are circular or unfalsifiable.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — urgency-dependency clarity; BP.12 candidate — false-urgency-necessity risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not claim urgency is inevitable or unconditional. Must not treat dependency completeness as urgency validation.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if discovery shows different urgency dependency conditions or workflow changes alter urgency pathways.
nodes.notes_limitations: Urgency dependency map governs which urgency conditions are necessary vs contingent; overclaiming unconditional urgency is a primary prohibited pattern.

nodes.purpose: Define the evidence type, tier, source family, and sufficiency threshold required before strengthening urgency claims beyond candidate hypothesis status.
nodes.required_output: Urgency evidence requirements matrix: evidence tier per urgency claim, permitted source families, sufficiency thresholds, escalation routes.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: Architecture Governance Rules, Evidence Ladder, BP.3 source governance; evidence_tier_required: E1 for evidence-requirement architecture; sufficiency_threshold: each urgency claim type has documented evidence tier, source family, and sufficiency threshold; evidence_rationale: evidence requirements define proof burden; cannot_support: urgency validation, procurement readiness, demand, or PMF.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no evidence-requirements matrix. Support: completed matrix aligned with Evidence Ladder. Revise: if Evidence Ladder thresholds change. Invalidate: if requirements conflict with BP.3 governance.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — urgency-evidence-requirement completeness; BP.12 candidate — insufficient-tier risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat evidence requirements as urgency evidence. Must not infer urgency validation from governance architecture.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if Evidence Ladder changes, BP.3 governance shifts, or urgency claim types expand.
nodes.notes_limitations: Evidence requirements defined here feed BP.2.6.2; urgency claims require higher-tier evidence than problem definition claims.

nodes.purpose: Define all conclusions that BP.2.3 urgency evidence must never support, regardless of evidence quantity.
nodes.required_output: Prohibited-inference register for urgency: each prohibited conclusion, urgency component it protects, and escalation trigger if violated.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: Architecture Governance Rules, BP.2.6 evidence standards; evidence_tier_required: E1 for prohibited-inference architecture; sufficiency_threshold: all prohibited urgency inferences are explicitly documented and exhaustive; evidence_rationale: prohibitions protect urgency architecture from demand, WTP, and procurement overclaiming; cannot_support: WTP, procurement readiness, adoption, PMF, budget availability, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: prohibition register not populated. Support: completed prohibition matrix. Revise: if new prohibited patterns emerge. Invalidate: if prohibitions are internally contradictory.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — prohibited-urgency-inference completeness; BP.12 candidate — implicit-urgency-overclaim risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not allow urgency evidence to support demand, WTP, or procurement readiness claims. Must not treat urgency as proof of buyer intent.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if BP.2.6 standards change, new prohibited patterns emerge, or narrative implies prohibited urgency claims.
nodes.notes_limitations: Prohibited inference register governs cross-domain leakage from urgency to demand or WTP; most common overclaim vector in early-stage problem narratives.

nodes.purpose: Confirm that BP.2.3 is internally coherent, complete, and free of prohibited inferences before why-now and hypothesis architecture proceeds.
nodes.required_output: Acceptance checklist: urgency definition, priority criteria, timing triggers, stakeholder urgency map, assumptions, dependencies, evidence requirements, and prohibited inferences are present, coherent, and non-contradictory.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: completed BP.2.3.1–BP.2.3.8, architecture audit, controller review; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: BP.2.3.1–BP.2.3.8 are complete, coherent, non-contradictory, and free of prohibited inferences; evidence_rationale: acceptance check verifies architecture coherence only; cannot_support: urgency validation, demand, WTP, procurement readiness, PMF, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: controller approval not recorded. Support: completed architecture review. Revise: if any BP.2.3 child changes. Invalidate: if contradictions remain.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — urgency-acceptance gap; BP.12 candidate — architecture-coherence risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat urgency-architecture acceptance as urgency validation, demand evidence, or buyer intent proof.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if any BP.2.3 child changes, discovery contradicts urgency architecture, or BP.6 reveals different priority signals.
nodes.notes_limitations: Architecture-only gate; urgency hypothesis requires separate discovery and priority evidence before it can be strengthened.

nodes.purpose: Defines the hypothesised timing logic explaining why the problem may matter now rather than later.
nodes.required_output: Why-now hypothesis; timing drivers; external/internal trigger map; evidence requirements; prohibited timing inferences.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: BP.3-governed external sources, user discovery, institutional evidence, product-context assumptions; evidence_tier_required: E1 for candidate why-now logic, E3+ for external timing facts, E4+ for user-perceived timing, E6+ for institutional timing pressure; sufficiency_threshold: timing drivers are separately sourced and not treated as demand evidence; evidence_rationale: why-now logic governs timing claims but cannot validate market pull; cannot_support: market growth, adoption, procurement readiness, willingness to pay, PMF, or investor timing claims.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Assumes timing drivers may be relevant but unvalidated. Gap: no governed why-now evidence populated. Support: sourced external changes, user-perceived timing pressure, or institutional trigger evidence. Revise if timing drivers are weak, stale, or unrelated to buyer behaviour.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — why-now evidence gap; BP.12 candidate — timing-driver overclaim risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not infer demand, market readiness, category growth, procurement readiness, or investor attractiveness from timing drivers alone.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if external timing drivers change, sources become stale, or discovery shows timing is not salient to users or buyers.
nodes.notes_limitations: Why-now is a hypothesis, not market validation.

nodes.purpose: Define the environmental, technological, institutional, or behavioural factors hypothesised to make the governed problem more salient now than before.
nodes.required_output: Timing driver register: driver label, driver type (technological/regulatory/behavioural/institutional), proposed causal mechanism linking driver to problem salience, and evidence tier required.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: BP.3-governed external sources, founder hypothesis, external-context analysis; evidence_tier_required: E1 for driver identification, E3+ for sourced timing-driver facts, E4+ for user-perceived timing salience; sufficiency_threshold: timing drivers are sourced, specific, and linked to the governed problem rather than to general market conditions; evidence_rationale: timing driver architecture establishes what external evidence must be gathered; cannot_support: market growth, adoption, procurement readiness, WTP, PMF, or investor timing claims.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no sourced timing-driver evidence. Support: BP.3-governed external sources confirming driver existence. Revise: if drivers are weak, stale, or unrelated to user behaviour. Invalidate: if no timing driver can be linked to problem salience.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — timing-driver evidence gap; BP.12 candidate — timing-driver overclaim risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not infer market readiness, category growth, procurement urgency, or investor attractiveness from timing drivers alone.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if external timing drivers change, sources become stale, or discovery shows timing is not salient to users or buyers.
nodes.notes_limitations: Timing drivers must reference BP.3-governed external sources; internal assumptions about external drivers are prohibited without source governance.

nodes.purpose: Identify the product-internal or founder-internal conditions that create a timing rationale for acting on the problem now.
nodes.required_output: Internal trigger register: trigger type (product readiness, founder availability, resource alignment, competitive window), mechanism, current status, and validation requirement.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: canonical_product_context, internal_architecture, founder hypothesis; evidence_tier_required: E1 for internal trigger identification; sufficiency_threshold: internal triggers are explicit, distinct from external drivers, and not treated as market-pull evidence; evidence_rationale: internal trigger architecture separates supply-side timing from demand-side timing; cannot_support: demand, market readiness, buyer urgency, PMF, procurement readiness, or investor attractiveness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: internal trigger register not formalised. Support: internal product status and resource-alignment documentation. Revise: if internal readiness changes. Invalidate: if internal triggers are not genuinely distinct from external drivers.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — internal-trigger clarity; BP.12 candidate — supply-demand-conflation risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat internal readiness or competitive opportunity as demand-side evidence. Must not conflate "we are ready now" with "buyers need it now".
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if product readiness, resource alignment, or competitive context changes.
nodes.notes_limitations: Internal triggers (product readiness, founder availability) are not demand-side evidence; their presence does not imply market timing.

nodes.purpose: Identify the external events, regulatory changes, technological shifts, or market conditions that constitute timing pressure from outside the product.
nodes.required_output: External trigger register: trigger event, trigger source (regulatory/technological/competitive/behavioural), salience to governed problem, evidence required, source family.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: BP.3-governed external sources, regulatory landscape, technology trend sources, competitor intelligence; evidence_tier_required: E1 for trigger identification, E3+ for sourced trigger evidence, E4+ for user-perceived external pressure; sufficiency_threshold: external triggers are sourced, recent, and linked to the governed problem rather than background market noise; evidence_rationale: external trigger architecture ensures why-now logic is grounded in verifiable events; cannot_support: market growth, adoption, PMF, procurement readiness, WTP, or investor timing claims.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no sourced external trigger evidence. Support: BP.3-governed sources confirming trigger events. Revise: if triggers are background noise rather than problem-salient events. Invalidate: if no external trigger links to the governed problem.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — external-trigger evidence gap; BP.12 candidate — market-noise conflation risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not infer market momentum, category growth, or buyer urgency from external trigger identification alone.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if external landscape changes, sources become stale, or user discovery shows triggers are not salient.
nodes.notes_limitations: External triggers require BP.3-governed source evidence; unverified claims about regulatory shifts or technology adoption are prohibited.

nodes.purpose: State all unvalidated assumptions underpinning the why-now hypothesis, labelled as unvalidated with falsification conditions.
nodes.required_output: Why-now assumption register: each assumption, the timing component it supports, labelled as unvalidated, with support/revise/invalidate triggers.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: internal architecture, founder hypothesis, assumption ledger; evidence_tier_required: E1 for candidate assumption register, E3+ for external validation evidence; sufficiency_threshold: all timing assumptions are explicit, labelled as unvalidated, and falsifiable; evidence_rationale: assumption governance prevents hidden timing overclaiming; cannot_support: timing validity, market salience, buyer urgency, demand, or PMF.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: assumption register not formalised. Support: completed assumption ledger with falsification conditions. Revise: if evidence validates or contradicts assumptions. Invalidate: if assumptions are unstated.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — why-now assumption completeness; BP.12 candidate — hidden-timing-assumption risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat timing assumption completeness as validation. Must not present timing assumptions as market facts.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if external drivers change, internal readiness shifts, or discovery contradicts timing assumptions.
nodes.notes_limitations: Why-now assumptions are among the most speculative in the architecture; all must carry falsification conditions and BP.12 routing.

nodes.purpose: Identify the upstream conditions and architectural dependencies that must be satisfied for the why-now logic to be coherent.
nodes.required_output: Timing dependency map: timing component × prerequisite condition × dependency type × evidence required.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: internal architecture, BP.2.1–BP.2.4 child nodes, external source evidence; evidence_tier_required: E1 for dependency architecture, E3+ for evidence of dependency conditions; sufficiency_threshold: all timing dependencies are explicit and non-circular; evidence_rationale: dependency mapping prevents timing claims that outrun their conditions; cannot_support: timing inevitability, market readiness, PMF, or procurement readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: dependency map not formalised. Support: confirmed dependency conditions. Revise: if conditions are missing or different. Invalidate: if dependencies are circular or unfalsifiable.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — timing-dependency clarity; BP.12 candidate — false-timing-necessity risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not claim timing pressure is inevitable, universal, or self-sustaining without evidenced dependency conditions.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if external landscape changes, internal readiness shifts, or dependency conditions become unconfirmable.
nodes.notes_limitations: Timing dependency map prevents circular why-now logic where the product's existence is cited as the reason the market is ready.

nodes.purpose: Define alternative why-now explanations that could equally explain the timing logic, preventing premature commitment to one timing narrative.
