nodes.required_output: Alternative timing hypothesis register: alternative explanation, evidence required to distinguish from primary hypothesis, probability label (candidate/less-likely/ruled-out), rationale.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: internal architecture, external source evidence, discovery evidence; evidence_tier_required: E1 for alternative hypothesis identification, E3+ for distinguishing evidence; sufficiency_threshold: at least two alternative timing hypotheses are documented with distinguishing evidence requirements; evidence_rationale: alternative hypothesis architecture prevents premature timing commitment and supports intellectual honesty; cannot_support: alternative validation, market timing certainty, demand, or PMF.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: alternative hypotheses not documented. Support: explicit alternatives with distinguishing evidence. Revise: if new alternative explanations emerge or primary hypothesis is weakened. Invalidate: if alternatives are not genuinely distinct.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — alternative-hypothesis completeness; BP.12 candidate — timing-lock-in risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat alternative hypothesis documentation as evidence for any single timing narrative.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if discovery or external evidence supports an alternative timing hypothesis or new alternatives emerge.
nodes.notes_limitations: Alternative timing hypotheses must be documented before the primary timing narrative is used in investor or GTM materials.

nodes.purpose: Define the evidence type, tier, source family, and sufficiency threshold required before strengthening why-now claims beyond candidate hypothesis status.
nodes.required_output: Why-now evidence requirements matrix: evidence tier per timing claim, permitted source families, sufficiency thresholds, escalation routes to BP.3, BP.6, and BP.12.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: Architecture Governance Rules, Evidence Ladder, BP.3 source governance; evidence_tier_required: E1 for evidence-requirement architecture; sufficiency_threshold: each timing claim type has documented evidence tier, source family, and sufficiency threshold; evidence_rationale: evidence requirements define proof burden before timing claim strengthening; cannot_support: timing validation, market readiness, demand, or PMF.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no evidence-requirements matrix. Support: completed matrix aligned with Evidence Ladder. Revise: if thresholds change. Invalidate: if requirements conflict with BP.3.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — why-now evidence-requirement completeness; BP.12 candidate — insufficient-tier risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat evidence requirements as timing evidence. Must not infer validation from governance.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if Evidence Ladder changes, BP.3 shifts, or timing claim types expand.
nodes.notes_limitations: Why-now evidence requirements are typically higher tier than problem-definition requirements; external sources require BP.3.3 academic/industry governance.

nodes.purpose: Define all conclusions that BP.2.4 why-now evidence must never support, regardless of evidence quantity.
nodes.required_output: Prohibited-inference register for timing: each prohibited conclusion, timing component it protects, and escalation trigger if violated.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: Architecture Governance Rules, BP.2.6 evidence standards; evidence_tier_required: E1 for prohibited-inference architecture; sufficiency_threshold: all prohibited timing inferences are explicitly documented and exhaustive; evidence_rationale: prohibitions protect timing architecture from demand, market growth, and procurement overclaiming; cannot_support: market growth, adoption, WTP, procurement readiness, PMF, investor timing attractiveness, or category expansion.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: prohibition register not populated. Support: completed prohibition matrix. Revise: if new prohibited patterns emerge. Invalidate: if prohibitions are contradictory.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — prohibited-timing-inference completeness; BP.12 candidate — implicit-timing-overclaim risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not allow timing evidence to support market growth, demand, WTP, or procurement readiness claims.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if BP.2.6 standards change, new prohibited patterns emerge, or narrative implies prohibited timing claims.
nodes.notes_limitations: Prohibited timing inferences are the primary guard against investor-narrative overclaiming from external trend data.

nodes.purpose: Confirm that BP.2.4 is internally coherent, complete, and free of prohibited inferences before governing hypothesis and validation design proceed.
nodes.required_output: Acceptance checklist: timing drivers, internal triggers, external triggers, assumptions, dependencies, alternative hypotheses, evidence requirements, and prohibited inferences are present, coherent, and non-contradictory.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: completed BP.2.4.1–BP.2.4.8, architecture audit, controller review; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: BP.2.4.1–BP.2.4.8 are complete, coherent, non-contradictory, and free of prohibited inferences; evidence_rationale: acceptance check verifies architecture coherence only; cannot_support: timing validation, market readiness, demand, WTP, PMF, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: controller approval not recorded. Support: completed architecture review. Revise: if any BP.2.4 child changes. Invalidate: if contradictions remain.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — why-now acceptance gap; BP.12 candidate — timing-coherence risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat why-now architecture acceptance as timing validation, market-readiness evidence, or investor proof.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if any BP.2.4 child changes, external landscape changes, or discovery contradicts the why-now hypothesis.
nodes.notes_limitations: Architecture-only gate; why-now remains a hypothesis until external evidence and discovery corroborate the timing logic.

nodes.purpose: Defines the central falsifiable hypothesis that BP.1–BP.11 must test without treating it as evidence.
nodes.required_output: Governing hypothesis statement; falsification conditions; evidence path links; dependency map; prohibited upgrades; hypothesis acceptance check.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: founder-authored scope input, BP.1 product/workflow architecture, BP.10 validation design; evidence_tier_required: E1 for candidate hypothesis statement, E4+ for behavioural support, E6+ for institutional workflow support, E7 only for repeated validated workflow behaviour if claimed; sufficiency_threshold: hypothesis is falsifiable, bounded, linked to validation dependencies, and not presented as proven; evidence_rationale: the governing hypothesis coordinates validation architecture; cannot_support: PMF, adoption, institutional behaviour, commercial readiness, or validated product claim before evidence exists.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Assumes the governing hypothesis can be stated before validation. Gap: no validation evidence populated. Support: BP.10 pilot evidence and behavioural/institutional evidence. Revise if BP.1 scope, BP.6 discovery, or BP.10 validation design changes the testable claim.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — governing-hypothesis uncertainty; BP.12 candidate — premature-hypothesis-upgrade risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not present the governing hypothesis as evidence, PMF, validated adoption, repeated behaviour, institutional workflow change, or commercial proof.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if product scope changes, validation design changes, pilot evidence contradicts the hypothesis, or the hypothesis becomes unfalsifiable.
nodes.notes_limitations: The governing hypothesis is a test object, not a validated conclusion.

nodes.purpose: State the single, central, falsifiable governing hypothesis in one bounded sentence that coordinates all downstream BP validation.
nodes.required_output: Governing hypothesis statement: one sentence naming the hypothesised behaviour, actor, workflow, and condition under which the product claim would be true.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: founder-authored scope input, BP.1 product/workflow architecture, BP.2.1–BP.2.4 problem architecture; evidence_tier_required: E1 for candidate hypothesis statement, E4+ for behavioural support evidence, E6+ for institutional workflow support; sufficiency_threshold: hypothesis is a single falsifiable sentence bounded to a specific actor, workflow, and testable condition and is not presented as evidence, fact, or validated claim; evidence_rationale: the hypothesis statement defines what BP.10 validation must test; cannot_support: PMF, adoption, institutional behaviour, commercial readiness, or validated product claim before evidence exists.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no controller-approved hypothesis wording. Support: BP.10 pilot evidence and behavioural/institutional evidence. Revise: if BP.1 scope, BP.6 discovery, or BP.10 validation design changes the testable claim. Invalidate: if hypothesis is not falsifiable or contradicts BP.1 product scope.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — hypothesis-statement falsifiability; BP.12 candidate — hypothesis-wording overclaim risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not present the hypothesis as evidence, validated claim, PMF, repeated behaviour, or institutional acceptance. Must not conflate candidate hypothesis with proven product-market fit.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if product scope changes, problem definition changes, validation design changes, or BP.10 pilot evidence contradicts the hypothesis.
nodes.notes_limitations: Hypothesis statement is the single most important governance object in BP.2; any change requires re-audit of all BP.2.5 children and cascades to BP.10.

nodes.purpose: Define the specific, observable conditions under which the governing hypothesis would be considered falsified.
nodes.required_output: Falsification condition register: falsification criterion, observable signal, evidence tier required to trigger falsification, and consequence for BP architecture if falsified.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: BP.1 product/workflow architecture, BP.10 validation design, internal architecture; evidence_tier_required: E1 for falsification architecture; sufficiency_threshold: each falsification condition is specific, observable, and linked to the hypothesis component it governs; evidence_rationale: falsification conditions prevent unfalsifiable hypothesis entrenchment; cannot_support: hypothesis validity, PMF, demand, adoption, or commercial readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: falsification conditions not formalised. Support: completed falsification register linked to BP.10 pilot design. Revise: if hypothesis changes or pilot design introduces new testable conditions. Invalidate: if falsification conditions are circular, vague, or unlinked to observable signals.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — falsification-condition completeness; BP.12 candidate — unfalsifiable-hypothesis risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat absence of falsification as confirmation. Must not define falsification conditions that cannot be observed in a realistic pilot or discovery setting.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if hypothesis statement changes, pilot design changes, or falsification signals become unobservable.
nodes.notes_limitations: Falsification conditions must be observable and testable through BP.10 pilot design; unfalsifiable conditions are prohibited.

nodes.purpose: Map each hypothesis component to the downstream BP domain responsible for generating the evidence required to test it.
nodes.required_output: Evidence path map: hypothesis component × BP domain (BP.6, BP.10, BP.3) × evidence tier required × evidence type × sufficiency threshold.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: internal architecture, BP.3 source governance, BP.6 discovery design, BP.10 validation design; evidence_tier_required: E1 for evidence path architecture; sufficiency_threshold: every hypothesis component has an explicit evidence path and responsible BP domain; evidence_rationale: path mapping prevents orphaned hypothesis components that cannot be tested; cannot_support: hypothesis validation, PMF, adoption, demand, or commercial readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: evidence paths not mapped. Support: completed dependency map aligned with BP.6, BP.10, and BP.3. Revise: if responsible BP domains change or evidence requirements shift. Invalidate: if any hypothesis component has no evidence path.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — evidence-path completeness; BP.12 candidate — orphaned-hypothesis-component risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat evidence path definition as evidence itself. Must not infer hypothesis validity from evidence path completeness.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if BP.3, BP.6, or BP.10 scope changes, or if new hypothesis components emerge.
nodes.notes_limitations: Evidence path links are the structural bridge between BP.2 hypothesis and BP.3/BP.6/BP.10 evidence architecture; orphaned hypothesis components are a blocking gap.

nodes.purpose: Identify all upstream architecture nodes and downstream validation domains that the governing hypothesis depends on for coherence.
nodes.required_output: Hypothesis dependency register: upstream dependency × dependency type (necessary/sufficient) × downstream validation dependency × reopen trigger if dependency changes.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: BP.1 product/workflow architecture, BP.2.1–BP.2.4, BP.10 validation design; evidence_tier_required: E1 for dependency architecture; sufficiency_threshold: all upstream and downstream dependencies are explicit and non-circular; evidence_rationale: dependency mapping prevents hypothesis claims that outrun their architectural conditions; cannot_support: hypothesis validity, PMF, adoption, demand, or commercial readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: dependency register not formalised. Support: completed dependency register aligned with BP.1–BP.2 and BP.10. Revise: if upstream architecture changes. Invalidate: if dependencies are circular or create unfalsifiable conditions.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — hypothesis-dependency clarity; BP.12 candidate — circular-dependency risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat dependency completeness as hypothesis support. Must not create circular dependencies that prevent falsification.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if BP.1 scope, BP.2 problem architecture, or BP.10 validation design changes.
nodes.notes_limitations: Hypothesis dependency map must not contain circular dependencies; founding assumptions cannot simultaneously support the hypothesis and depend on it.

nodes.purpose: State all unvalidated assumptions underpinning the governing hypothesis, labelled as unvalidated with explicit falsification conditions.
nodes.required_output: Hypothesis assumption register: each assumption, the hypothesis component it supports, labelled as unvalidated, with support/revise/invalidate triggers and evidence tier required.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: internal architecture, founder hypothesis, assumption ledger; evidence_tier_required: E1 for candidate assumption register, E4+ for assumption-validation evidence; sufficiency_threshold: all governing hypothesis assumptions are explicit, labelled as unvalidated, and falsifiable; evidence_rationale: assumption governance prevents hidden overclaiming in the governing hypothesis; cannot_support: hypothesis validity, PMF, adoption, demand, or commercial readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: assumption register not formalised. Support: completed assumption ledger with falsification conditions. Revise: if discovery or pilot evidence validates or contradicts assumptions. Invalidate: if assumptions are unstated or non-falsifiable.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — hypothesis-assumption completeness; BP.12 candidate — hidden-hypothesis-assumption risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat hypothesis assumption completeness as validation. Must not present hypothesis assumptions as evidence or confirmed observations.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if discovery validates, revises, or invalidates any hypothesis assumption, or new assumptions are identified.
nodes.notes_limitations: Hypothesis assumptions are more consequential than section-level assumptions; they govern the entire validation design in BP.10.

nodes.purpose: Define the conditions under which the governing hypothesis must NOT be upgraded to a stronger claim, regardless of partial or anecdotal evidence.
nodes.required_output: Prohibited upgrade register: prohibited upgrade type, evidence threshold not yet met, trigger condition requiring escalation to BP.12, and consequence of premature upgrade.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: Architecture Governance Rules, Evidence Ladder, BP.3 source governance, BP.10 validation design; evidence_tier_required: E1 for prohibited-upgrade architecture; sufficiency_threshold: all prohibited upgrade patterns are explicitly documented and exhaustive; evidence_rationale: prohibited upgrades prevent premature PMF, adoption, and commercial-readiness claims from a candidate hypothesis; cannot_support: PMF, repeated behaviour, institutional adoption, validated demand, or investor readiness before required evidence tiers are met.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: prohibited upgrade register not populated. Support: completed register aligned with Evidence Ladder. Revise: if new prohibited upgrade patterns emerge. Invalidate: if prohibitions are internally contradictory.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — prohibited-upgrade completeness; BP.12 candidate — premature-hypothesis-upgrade risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not allow hypothesis upgrade to PMF, adoption, or validated claim without E4+/E6+/E7 evidence as required. Must not treat positive pilot signals as hypothesis validation.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if Evidence Ladder thresholds change, BP.10 produces partial evidence, or narrative implies premature hypothesis upgrade.
nodes.notes_limitations: Prohibited hypothesis upgrades are the governance mechanism preventing premature PMF, adoption, or validation claims; this node has escalation authority.

nodes.purpose: Define the evidence type, tier, source family, and sufficiency threshold required to move the governing hypothesis from candidate to supported, and from supported to validated.
nodes.required_output: Hypothesis evidence requirements matrix: upgrade stage (candidate → supported → validated) × evidence tier × source family × sufficiency threshold × escalation route.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: Architecture Governance Rules, Evidence Ladder, BP.3 source governance, BP.10 validation design; evidence_tier_required: E1 for evidence-requirement architecture; sufficiency_threshold: each hypothesis upgrade stage has explicit evidence tier, source family, and sufficiency threshold; evidence_rationale: staged evidence requirements prevent premature hypothesis upgrades; cannot_support: hypothesis validation, PMF, adoption, demand, or commercial readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no evidence-requirements matrix. Support: completed matrix aligned with Evidence Ladder and BP.10. Revise: if Evidence Ladder thresholds change. Invalidate: if requirements conflict with BP.3 or BP.10.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — hypothesis-evidence-requirement completeness; BP.12 candidate — insufficient-tier risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat evidence requirements as hypothesis evidence. Must not infer validation from governance architecture.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if Evidence Ladder changes, BP.10 design shifts, or hypothesis upgrade stages are revised.
nodes.notes_limitations: Evidence requirements here define the upgrade path from candidate hypothesis to supported hypothesis; no upgrade permitted below the required tier.

nodes.node_title: Prohibited Hypothesis Claims and Inference Patterns
nodes.purpose: Define all conclusions that governing hypothesis architecture must never support, regardless of evidence quantity or source quality.
nodes.required_output: Prohibited-inference register for governing hypothesis: each prohibited conclusion, the hypothesis component it protects, and escalation trigger if violated.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: Architecture Governance Rules, BP.2.6 evidence standards, BP.1.2 non-scope; evidence_tier_required: E1 for prohibited-inference architecture; sufficiency_threshold: all prohibited hypothesis inferences are explicitly documented and exhaustive; evidence_rationale: prohibitions prevent the governing hypothesis from being treated as proof of PMF, adoption, demand, or commercial readiness; cannot_support: PMF, adoption, institutional behaviour, commercial readiness, investor readiness, validated demand, or repeated usage claims.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: prohibition register not populated. Support: completed prohibition matrix aligned with BP.2.6. Revise: if new prohibited patterns emerge. Invalidate: if prohibitions are internally contradictory.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — prohibited-hypothesis-inference completeness; BP.12 candidate — implicit-overclaim risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not allow hypothesis evidence to support PMF, demand, adoption, institutional behaviour, or commercial readiness claims before required evidence tiers are met.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if BP.2.6 standards change, new prohibited patterns emerge, or narrative implies prohibited hypothesis claims.
nodes.notes_limitations: Prohibited inference patterns for the governing hypothesis are the most critical in BP.2; the hypothesis must remain a test object until BP.10 evidence warrants upgrade.

nodes.purpose: Confirm that BP.2.5 is internally coherent, complete, and free of prohibited inferences before downstream validation design and narrative constraints proceed.
nodes.required_output: Acceptance checklist: hypothesis statement, falsification conditions, evidence path links, dependency map, assumptions, prohibited upgrades, evidence requirements, and prohibited inferences are present, coherent, and non-contradictory.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: completed BP.2.5.1–BP.2.5.8, architecture audit, controller review; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: BP.2.5.1–BP.2.5.8 are complete, coherent, non-contradictory, and free of prohibited inferences; evidence_rationale: acceptance check verifies architecture coherence only; cannot_support: hypothesis validation, PMF, adoption, demand, WTP, procurement readiness, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: controller approval not recorded. Support: completed architecture review. Revise: if any BP.2.5 child changes. Invalidate: if contradictions or unresolved prohibited claims remain.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — hypothesis-acceptance gap; BP.12 candidate — architecture-coherence risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat hypothesis-architecture acceptance as hypothesis validation, PMF evidence, demand proof, or investor readiness.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if any BP.2.5 child changes, BP.1 scope changes, BP.6 discovery contradicts hypothesis, or BP.10 pilot evidence challenges the governing hypothesis.
nodes.notes_limitations: Architecture-only gate; hypothesis acceptance means it is well-formed and falsifiable, not that it is true or validated.

nodes.purpose: Defines evidence standards for BP.2 problem, pain, urgency, why-now, consequence, and governing-hypothesis claims.
nodes.required_output: BP.2 evidence-use checklist; allowed claims by evidence tier; prohibited inference patterns; escalation routes to BP.3, BP.6, BP.10, and BP.12.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: Architecture Governance Rules, Evidence Ladder, Source Library where applicable, BP.3 source governance; evidence_tier_required: E1 for architecture standards, E4+ for behavioural problem claims, E6+ for institutional claims, E7 for repeated behaviour claims if asserted; sufficiency_threshold: every BP.2 claim type has evidence tier, sufficiency threshold, cannot-support boundary, and BP.12 escalation route; evidence_rationale: BP.2 requires local evidence discipline without replacing BP.3; cannot_support: final claim validation, PMF, procurement readiness, compliance, feasibility, investor readiness, or commercial traction.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Assumes BP.3 remains source-governance owner and BP.10 remains validation owner. Gap: BP.2 evidence matrix not populated. Support: accepted BP.2 claim-evidence matrix. Revise if evidence ladder or source-routing rules change.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — BP.2 evidence-standard gap; BP.12 candidate — problem-claim source-misuse risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not replace BP.3 source governance or BP.10 validation logic. Must not infer demand, WTP, procurement readiness, PMF, compliance, feasibility, or investor readiness from problem evidence alone.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if BP.3 evidence rules, evidence ladder thresholds, BP.2 claim types, or BP.10 validation requirements change.
nodes.notes_limitations: Governs BP.2-local evidence discipline only; does not populate evidence.

nodes.purpose: Define the classes of claims made within BP.2 and assign each claim type to a governed evidence category, distinguishing problem, pain, urgency, why-now, and hypothesis claims.
nodes.required_output: BP.2 claim classification matrix: claim type, claim domain (BP.2.1–BP.2.5), evidence category, and routing to evidence tier and source family.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: Architecture Governance Rules, BP.2.1–BP.2.5 child nodes, Evidence Ladder; evidence_tier_required: E1 for claim classification architecture; sufficiency_threshold: all BP.2 claim types are uniquely classified and mapped to evidence tiers without conflating claim domains; evidence_rationale: claim classification governs evidence standards and prevents cross-domain inference; cannot_support: claim validity, demand, PMF, urgency, or commercial readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no formal BP.2 claim taxonomy. Support: completed claim classification matrix aligned with BP.2 child nodes. Revise: if new BP.2 claim types emerge. Invalidate: if claim classifications conflict with BP.2 child-node boundaries.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — BP.2-claim-classification completeness; BP.12 candidate — cross-domain-inference risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not conflate problem claims with urgency claims, urgency claims with demand claims, or why-now claims with market-readiness claims.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if new BP.2 claim types emerge or claim classifications conflict with BP.2 child nodes.
nodes.notes_limitations: Claim classification is the prerequisite for all downstream evidence tier and source routing governance; ungrouped claims cannot be governed.

nodes.node_title: Evidence Tier Requirements by Claim Type
nodes.purpose: Define the minimum evidence tier required for each BP.2 claim type before the claim may be presented as supported.
nodes.required_output: Evidence-tier matrix: BP.2 claim type × minimum evidence tier × escalation tier for stronger claims × cannot-support boundary.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: Evidence Ladder, Architecture Governance Rules, BP.3 source governance; evidence_tier_required: E1 for tier-requirement architecture; sufficiency_threshold: each BP.2 claim type has an assigned minimum tier; no claim may be strengthened without meeting the required tier; evidence_rationale: tier mapping prevents unsupported problem, pain, urgency, and hypothesis claims; cannot_support: claim validity, demand, PMF, adoption, urgency, or commercial readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no tier-mapping document. Support: completed tier matrix aligned with Evidence Ladder. Revise: if Evidence Ladder thresholds change. Invalidate: if tier requirements conflict with BP.3 standards.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — evidence-tier mismatch; BP.12 candidate — insufficient-tier risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not allow any BP.2 claim to be strengthened below its required evidence tier. Must not treat tier assignment as claim validation.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if Evidence Ladder changes, BP.3 tier standards shift, or BP.2 claim types change.
nodes.notes_limitations: Evidence tier requirements must be consistent with the Evidence Ladder; this node is the primary enforcement point for tier discipline across BP.2.

nodes.purpose: Define which evidence source families may support each BP.2 claim type and when evidence must be routed to BP.3 for source governance.
nodes.required_output: Source-routing matrix: BP.2 claim type × approved source family × prohibited source substitutions × routing rule (local/BP.3).
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: Source Library, Evidence Ladder, BP.3 source governance, Architecture Governance Rules; evidence_tier_required: E1 for routing architecture; sufficiency_threshold: all BP.2 claim types have explicit approved source families and routing rules; evidence_rationale: source routing prevents BP.3 authority dilution and source misuse; cannot_support: claim validity, demand, PMF, urgency, or commercial readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no routing matrix. Support: completed source-routing architecture aligned with Source Library and BP.3. Revise: if Source Library or BP.3 governance changes. Invalidate: if routing rules conflict with BP.3.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — source-routing ambiguity; BP.12 candidate — prohibited-source-use risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not substitute sources without BP.3 approval. Must not use prohibited sources. Must not infer claim validity from source approval alone.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if Source Library changes, BP.3 governance shifts, or new evidence sources emerge for BP.2 claims.
nodes.notes_limitations: Source routing matrix governs which source families are permitted per claim type; substituting sources without BP.3 approval is a prohibited pattern.

nodes.purpose: Define the sufficiency threshold at each evidence stage (insufficient / sufficient-for-draft / sufficient-for-claim) for each BP.2 claim type.
nodes.required_output: Sufficiency threshold register: BP.2 claim type × evidence stage × threshold criteria × required evidence count and diversity × escalation condition.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: Evidence Ladder, Architecture Governance Rules, BP.3 source governance, BP.10 validation design; evidence_tier_required: E1 for threshold architecture; sufficiency_threshold: each BP.2 claim type has a documented sufficiency threshold for each evidence stage; evidence_rationale: threshold governance prevents premature claim strengthening and protects against n=1 generalisation; cannot_support: claim validity, demand, PMF, adoption, or commercial readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: sufficiency thresholds not defined per BP.2 claim type. Support: completed threshold register aligned with Evidence Ladder. Revise: if Evidence Ladder or BP.10 design changes. Invalidate: if thresholds are internally inconsistent or create unreachable standards.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — sufficiency-threshold clarity; BP.12 candidate — premature-claim-strengthening risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not advance a BP.2 claim beyond a threshold without meeting the required evidence stage. Must not treat single-source evidence as sufficient for institutional or population-level claims.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if Evidence Ladder, BP.3, or BP.10 thresholds change, or if new claim types create unspecified thresholds.
nodes.notes_limitations: Sufficiency thresholds define the graduation path for BP.2 claims; no claim may advance stages without meeting the documented threshold.

nodes.purpose: Define the explicit list of conclusions that no amount of BP.2 evidence — at any tier — may ever be used to support.
nodes.required_output: Cannot-support register: prohibited conclusion, governing BP.2 claim domain, rationale, and escalation trigger if violated.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: Architecture Governance Rules, BP.1.2 non-scope, BP.2.1–BP.2.5 evidence requirements; evidence_tier_required: E1 for cannot-support architecture; sufficiency_threshold: all cannot-support conclusions are explicitly documented, non-redundant, and exhaustive across all BP.2 claim domains; evidence_rationale: cannot-support boundaries enforce the epistemic ceiling of problem-domain evidence; cannot_support: demand, WTP, procurement readiness, PMF, adoption, institutional acceptance, compliance, feasibility, investor readiness, or commercial traction from any BP.2 evidence alone.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: cannot-support register not populated. Support: completed register aligned with BP.1.2 and BP.2.6.1. Revise: if non-scope or claim domain boundaries change. Invalidate: if cannot-support conclusions are incomplete or contradictory.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — cannot-support-boundary completeness; BP.12 candidate — implicit-ceiling-breach risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not allow any BP.2 evidence to cross a cannot-support boundary regardless of evidence strength or source quality.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if BP.1.2 non-scope changes, new cannot-support conclusions emerge, or downstream narrative implies a ceiling breach.
nodes.notes_limitations: Cannot-support boundaries are absolute ceilings; no evidence strength, volume, or tier can permit a BP.2 claim to cross them.

nodes.purpose: Define all cross-domain inference patterns that BP.2 evidence must never be used to support, regardless of evidence quantity.
nodes.required_output: Prohibited-inference register: inference pattern, source claim domain, target prohibited conclusion, evidence that triggers re-escalation.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: Architecture Governance Rules, BP.2.1–BP.2.5 evidence standards; evidence_tier_required: E1 for prohibited-inference architecture; sufficiency_threshold: all cross-domain prohibited inference patterns are explicitly documented; evidence_rationale: inference prohibitions prevent problem-domain evidence from leaking into demand, commercial, and validation domains; cannot_support: demand, WTP, procurement readiness, PMF, adoption, institutional acceptance, compliance, feasibility, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: prohibited inference register not populated. Support: completed register. Revise: if new inference patterns emerge across BP.2 claim domains. Invalidate: if prohibitions are internally contradictory or create unworkable constraints.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — prohibited-inference completeness; BP.12 candidate — cross-domain-leak risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not allow pain evidence to support urgency claims. Must not allow urgency evidence to support demand claims. Must not allow why-now evidence to support PMF claims.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if new inference patterns emerge, BP.2 domains are restructured, or downstream narrative exploits an undocumented inference pathway.
nodes.notes_limitations: Prohibited inference patterns govern cross-domain leakage; pain evidence must not support urgency, urgency must not support demand, timing must not support PMF.

nodes.node_title: Escalation Routes to BP.3, BP.6, BP.10, and BP.12
nodes.purpose: Define when BP.2 evidence must be escalated to other BP domains rather than resolved locally, and specify the routing logic.
nodes.required_output: Escalation dependency map: BP.2 claim type × escalation trigger × target BP domain × escalation action.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: Architecture Governance Rules, BP.3 source governance, BP.6 discovery design, BP.10 validation design, BP.12 risk register; evidence_tier_required: E1 for escalation-route architecture; sufficiency_threshold: all escalation paths and triggers are explicitly mapped and non-ambiguous; evidence_rationale: escalation governance prevents orphaned evidence gaps and ensures prohibited claims trigger the correct remediation path; cannot_support: claim validity, demand, PMF, urgency, or commercial readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no escalation map. Support: completed dependency map aligned with BP.3, BP.6, BP.10, and BP.12. Revise: if downstream domains change scope. Invalidate: if escalation routes create circular dependencies.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — escalation-route ambiguity; BP.12 candidate — orphaned-evidence-gap risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not resolve escalated claims locally. Must not leave evidence gaps unrouted. Must not treat escalation completion as claim resolution.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if downstream domains change scope, new escalation triggers emerge, or BP.12 risk register changes.
nodes.notes_limitations: Escalation routes are required before BP.2 is used in any downstream narrative; unrouted gaps cannot be cited in GTM, investor, or business plan materials.

nodes.purpose: State all unvalidated assumptions underpinning the BP.2 evidence standards architecture, and document known gaps in the evidence governance framework.
nodes.required_output: Evidence standards assumption register: each assumption, the evidence standard it supports, labelled as unvalidated, with falsification condition and gap-remediation trigger.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: internal architecture, Architecture Governance Rules, assumption ledger; evidence_tier_required: E1 for candidate assumption register; sufficiency_threshold: all evidence standards assumptions are explicit, labelled as unvalidated, and linked to falsification conditions; evidence_rationale: assumption governance prevents hidden evidence-standard weaknesses from being exploited; cannot_support: evidence standard validity, claim validity, demand, PMF, or commercial readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: evidence standards assumption register not formalised. Support: completed assumption ledger aligned with BP.3 and Evidence Ladder. Revise: if Evidence Ladder or BP.3 governance changes. Invalidate: if assumptions are unstated or circular.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — evidence-standards-assumption completeness; BP.12 candidate — hidden-governance-gap risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat assumption completeness as evidence standard validation. Must not present governance assumptions as settled architecture.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if Evidence Ladder changes, BP.3 governance shifts, or new governance gaps are identified.
nodes.notes_limitations: Evidence standards assumptions feed BP.12; governance assumptions are as important to track as content assumptions.

nodes.purpose: Confirm that BP.2.6 evidence standards architecture is internally coherent, complete, and correctly aligned with BP.3 source governance before downstream architecture proceeds.
nodes.required_output: Acceptance checklist: claim classification, evidence tiers, source routing, sufficiency thresholds, cannot-support boundaries, prohibited inferences, escalation routes, and assumptions are present, coherent, non-contradictory, and aligned with BP.3.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: completed BP.2.6.1–BP.2.6.8, Architecture Governance Rules, BP.3 source governance, architecture audit, controller review; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: BP.2.6.1–BP.2.6.8 are complete, coherent, non-contradictory, and aligned with BP.3; evidence_rationale: acceptance check verifies governance architecture coherence only; cannot_support: claim validity, demand, PMF, urgency, adoption, or commercial readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: controller approval not recorded. Support: completed architecture review with no BP.3 conflicts. Revise: if any BP.2.6 child changes. Invalidate: if contradictions or BP.3 conflicts remain.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — evidence-standards-acceptance gap; BP.12 candidate — BP.3-conflict risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat evidence-standards acceptance as claim validation. Must not infer claim strength from governance approval.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if any BP.2.6 child changes, BP.3 governance shifts, or BP.2 evidence standards conflict with downstream domains.
nodes.notes_limitations: Architecture-only gate; evidence standards acceptance means the framework is sound, not that any evidence has been gathered.

nodes.purpose: Determines whether BP.2 is architecturally coherent enough to support downstream research, validation design, and narrative constraints.
nodes.required_output: BP.2 acceptance checklist; unresolved gaps; contradiction register; dependency audit; reopen triggers; BP.12 routing.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: completed BP.2 child nodes, architecture audit, controller review; evidence_tier_required: E1 for architecture acceptance; higher tiers required only for substantive problem, urgency, or hypothesis claims; sufficiency_threshold: BP.2.1–BP.2.6 are complete, non-contradictory, and free of prohibited claims; evidence_rationale: acceptance gate verifies architecture coherence, not business validity; cannot_support: validated problem, urgency, demand, PMF, adoption, WTP, procurement readiness, compliance, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Assumes BP.2 child nodes remain candidate until controller review. Gap: no completed BP.2 branch audit. Support: completed audit with no contradictions. Revise if child nodes conflict or missing evidence standards are found.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — BP.2 architecture-incompleteness risk; BP.12 candidate — BP.2 contradiction risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat BP.2 architecture acceptance as validation of problem severity, urgency, buyer demand, PMF, or investment readiness.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if any BP.2 child changes, BP.1 scope changes, BP.6 discovery contradicts BP.2, or BP.10 validation results challenge the governing hypothesis.
nodes.notes_limitations: Acceptance is architecture-only unless claim-specific evidence thresholds are later met.

nodes.purpose: Verify that all required BP.2 child nodes (BP.2.1–BP.2.6) are present, populated, and not left as empty shells.
nodes.required_output: Completeness audit checklist: each BP.2 section × required-output status × population status × gap flag.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: completed BP.2.1–BP.2.6 child nodes, internal architecture; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: BP.2.1–BP.2.6 are all present with required outputs populated; evidence_rationale: completeness audit prevents downstream reliance on unpopulated architecture nodes; cannot_support: node quality, claim validity, demand, PMF, urgency, or commercial readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no completeness audit conducted. Support: systematic review of BP.2.1–BP.2.6 against required-output specification. Revise: if nodes are found to be empty or incompletely populated. Invalidate: if any required BP.2 section is absent.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — BP.2-completeness risk; BP.12 candidate — empty-node risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat node presence as node quality. Must not treat completeness audit as claim validation.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if any BP.2 section is revised, emptied, or found to be an unpopulated shell.
nodes.notes_limitations: Completeness audit must be conducted before controller review; empty or stub nodes are a blocking failure condition.

nodes.purpose: Identify and document all detected internal contradictions between BP.2 child nodes, and record their resolution status.
nodes.required_output: Contradiction register: contradiction description, nodes in conflict, resolution status (open/resolved/deferred), resolution action, and escalation route if unresolved.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: completed BP.2.1–BP.2.6 child nodes, architecture audit; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: all detected contradictions are documented with resolution status; no open contradiction may block BP.2 acceptance without an explicit deferral decision; evidence_rationale: contradiction detection prevents downstream architecture from inheriting unresolved conflicts; cannot_support: contradiction resolution validity, claim validity, demand, PMF, or commercial readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no contradiction audit conducted. Support: systematic cross-node review of BP.2.1–BP.2.6. Revise: if new contradictions emerge. Invalidate: if contradictions remain unresolved without a controller-approved deferral.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — BP.2-contradiction risk; BP.12 candidate — unresolved-conflict risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat contradiction documentation as contradiction resolution. Must not proceed with unresolved contradictions without controller-approved deferral.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if any BP.2 child changes, new contradictions emerge, or a resolved contradiction is reopened.
nodes.notes_limitations: Contradiction register must surface conflicts before they propagate into GTM, investor, or business plan materials.

nodes.purpose: Verify that all declared dependencies within and between BP.2 child nodes are valid, non-circular, and satisfied.
nodes.required_output: Dependency audit report: each declared dependency × dependency type × status (satisfied/unsatisfied/circular) × remediation action.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: completed BP.2.1–BP.2.6 child nodes, dependency maps within each section, internal architecture; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: all declared dependencies are verified as non-circular and satisfied or have an explicit unsatisfied-dependency escalation route; evidence_rationale: dependency audit prevents downstream architecture from relying on unresolved upstream dependencies; cannot_support: dependency quality, claim validity, demand, PMF, or commercial readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no dependency audit conducted. Support: systematic dependency-graph review of BP.2.1–BP.2.6. Revise: if unsatisfied or circular dependencies are found. Invalidate: if any critical dependency cannot be satisfied without restructuring BP.2.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — BP.2-dependency risk; BP.12 candidate — circular-dependency risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat dependency audit completion as dependency satisfaction. Must not ignore unsatisfied dependencies.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if any BP.2 child dependency changes, new dependencies are added, or a satisfied dependency becomes unsatisfied.
nodes.notes_limitations: Dependency audit includes cross-branch dependencies to BP.3, BP.6, BP.10, and BP.12; internal-only audits are insufficient.

nodes.purpose: Confirm that no prohibited claim or inference pattern has been introduced into BP.2 child nodes across all sections.
nodes.required_output: Prohibited claims audit report: review scope, prohibited claims checked, violations found, violation location, remediation status.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: completed BP.2.1–BP.2.6 prohibited-claims nodes, BP.2.6 evidence standards, Architecture Governance Rules; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: all BP.2.x.8 prohibited-claims registers and BP.2.6.5–BP.2.6.6 cannot-support/inference registers are reviewed and no violations are found or are remediated; evidence_rationale: prohibited claims audit prevents overclaiming from propagating into downstream BP architecture; cannot_support: claim validity, demand, PMF, urgency, adoption, or commercial readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no prohibited claims audit conducted. Support: systematic review of all BP.2 prohibited-claims nodes and BP.2.6 standards. Revise: if violations are found. Invalidate: if violations are unresolved.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — BP.2-prohibited-claims risk; BP.12 candidate — overclaim-propagation risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat prohibited claims audit completion as claim validation. Must not allow any identified violation to remain unresolved.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if any BP.2 child node changes, new prohibited patterns are identified, or downstream narrative implies a previously cleared prohibited claim.
nodes.notes_limitations: Prohibited claims audit is the final guard before BP.2 content is used downstream; any identified violation requires escalation before proceeding.

nodes.purpose: Document all known evidence, architecture, and governance gaps across BP.2 that have not been resolved, with routing to BP.12.
nodes.required_output: Unresolved gaps register: gap description, affected BP.2 node, gap type (evidence/architecture/governance), BP.12 routing, resolution condition.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: completed BP.2.1–BP.2.6 child nodes, BP.2.6 evidence standards, BP.12 risk register; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: all known gaps are documented with BP.12 routing and resolution conditions; evidence_rationale: gap register prevents unresolved issues from being invisibly absorbed into downstream architecture; cannot_support: gap resolution, claim validity, demand, PMF, or commercial readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no gap register conducted. Support: systematic gap review of BP.2.1–BP.2.6 against required-output specifications and evidence standards. Revise: if new gaps are found. Invalidate: if gaps are left undocumented.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — BP.2-gap-documentation risk; BP.12 candidate — invisible-gap risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat gap documentation as gap resolution. Must not proceed without routing all gaps to BP.12.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if new gaps are identified, existing gaps change status, or BP.12 routing is revised.
nodes.notes_limitations: Unresolved gaps register feeds BP.12; gaps must be routed, not ignored or deferred without documentation.

nodes.purpose: Define the conditions under which a previously accepted BP.2 architecture must be reopened and re-audited.
nodes.required_output: Reopen trigger register: trigger condition, affected BP.2 section(s), trigger type (scope/evidence/discovery/validation), required action on trigger.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: completed BP.2.1–BP.2.6 reopen conditions, BP.6 discovery design, BP.10 validation design; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: all material reopen conditions across BP.2 are documented and linked to the responsible BP.2 section; evidence_rationale: reopen trigger governance prevents stale architecture from being inherited by downstream nodes; cannot_support: trigger inevitability, claim validity, demand, PMF, or commercial readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: reopen trigger register not consolidated. Support: collation of reopen conditions from BP.2.1–BP.2.6. Revise: if new trigger conditions emerge. Invalidate: if triggers are absent or non-actionable.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — reopen-trigger completeness; BP.12 candidate — stale-architecture risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat reopen trigger documentation as resolution. Must not ignore a triggered reopen condition.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if any BP.2 child node is revised, discovery evidence contradicts BP.2 architecture, or BP.10 validation challenges the governing hypothesis.
nodes.notes_limitations: Reopen triggers must be consolidated from all BP.2 child reopen conditions; a missing trigger is itself a gap.

nodes.purpose: Confirm that all BP.12-candidate risks, uncertainties, and gaps identified across BP.2 have been explicitly routed to the BP.12 risk register.
nodes.required_output: BP.12 routing confirmation log: BP.12-candidate item, source BP.2 node, routing status (routed/pending/deferred), BP.12 risk register reference.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: completed BP.2.1–BP.2.6 linked_uncertainties fields, BP.12 risk register, internal architecture; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: all BP.12-candidate items from BP.2 are confirmed as routed to BP.12 or have an explicit deferral decision; evidence_rationale: BP.12 routing confirms that identified risks are not left as orphaned candidates; cannot_support: risk resolution, claim validity, demand, PMF, or commercial readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no BP.12 routing confirmation. Support: systematic review of all linked_uncertainties entries across BP.2.1–BP.2.6. Revise: if new BP.12 candidates emerge. Invalidate: if any BP.12 candidate is unrouted without a deferral decision.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — BP.12-routing completeness; BP.12 candidate — orphaned-risk risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat BP.12 routing as risk resolution. Must not leave any BP.12 candidate unrouted or unacknowledged.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if new BP.12 candidates are identified, BP.12 register changes, or previously routed items are revised.
nodes.notes_limitations: BP.12 routing confirmation is required before any BP.2 claim is used in investor narrative, GTM, or business plan synthesis.

nodes.purpose: Define the constraints that accepted BP.2 architecture places on investor narrative, GTM narrative, and product narrative — preventing prohibited claims from entering downstream communication.
nodes.required_output: Narrative constraint register: constraint, source BP.2 prohibition, applicable narrative domain (investor/GTM/product/discovery), enforcement mechanism.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: BP.2.6 evidence standards, BP.2.x.8 prohibited-claims nodes, Architecture Governance Rules; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: all material prohibited claims from BP.2 are translated into explicit narrative constraints; evidence_rationale: narrative constraint governance prevents prohibited BP.2 inferences from re-entering the architecture through investor decks, GTM copy, or product positioning; cannot_support: narrative effectiveness, investor readiness, GTM readiness, demand, PMF, or commercial readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: narrative constraints not derived from BP.2 prohibited claims. Support: completed constraint register aligned with BP.2.6 and BP.2.x.8 nodes. Revise: if BP.2 prohibited claims change. Invalidate: if narrative constraints conflict with BP.2 evidence standards.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — narrative-constraint completeness; BP.12 candidate — prohibited-claim-reentry risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat narrative constraint documentation as narrative quality assurance. Must not allow any BP.2 prohibited claim to appear in investor, GTM, or product narrative.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if BP.2 prohibited claims change, new narrative domains are introduced, or an audit reveals a prohibited claim in downstream narrative.
nodes.notes_limitations: Downstream narrative constraints are derived from BP.2 prohibited claims; they govern what may and may not be said in BP.9, BP.10, and BP.11.

nodes.purpose: Determine whether BP.2 as a whole is architecturally coherent, gap-documented, contradiction-free, and sufficiently governed to support downstream BP.3–BP.11 architecture and narrative.
nodes.required_output: BP.2 acceptance decision record: completeness status, contradiction status, dependency status, prohibited claims status, gap documentation status, BP.12 routing status, narrative constraint status, controller decision, and reopen conditions.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: completed BP.2.7.1–BP.2.7.8, all BP.2.1–BP.2.6 child nodes, architecture audit, controller review; evidence_tier_required: E1 for architecture acceptance; higher tiers required only for substantive problem, urgency, or hypothesis claims asserted as more than candidate; sufficiency_threshold: BP.2.7.1–BP.2.7.8 are all satisfactory; no open contradiction, unrouted gap, or prohibited claim violation remains without a controller-approved deferral; evidence_rationale: acceptance gate verifies BP.2 architecture is coherent enough to constrain downstream research, validation, and narrative without misrepresenting its epistemic status; cannot_support: validated problem, urgency, demand, PMF, adoption, WTP, procurement readiness, compliance, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: no completed BP.2 branch audit. Support: completed audit with all BP.2.7.1–BP.2.7.8 checks satisfactory. Revise: if child nodes conflict or missing evidence standards are found. Invalidate: if open contradictions or prohibited claim violations remain without deferral.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — BP.2-architecture-acceptance risk; BP.12 candidate — BP.2-contradiction risk; BP.12 candidate — premature-acceptance risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat BP.2 architecture acceptance as validation of problem severity, urgency, buyer demand, PMF, adoption, or investment readiness. Must not allow acceptance to block BP.12 routing of unresolved gaps.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if any BP.2 child changes, BP.1 scope changes, BP.6 discovery contradicts BP.2, BP.10 validation challenges the governing hypothesis, or a previously cleared audit item is revised.
nodes.notes_limitations: BP.2 acceptance is architecture-only; it does not validate problem severity, urgency, demand, or buyer intent. Validation evidence routes to BP.6 and BP.10.

nodes.purpose: Governs source audit, source classification, evidence inventory, source-use boundaries, conflict flagging, and evidence-quality rules.
nodes.required_output: BP.3 Level 2 node set covering source inventory, evidence-tier classification, academic foundation, claim-support mapping, conflict/source-misuse controls, and evidence-governance acceptance check.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: internal_architecture, Source Library, Evidence Ladder, uploaded/governed sources; evidence_tier_required: E1 for architecture, higher tiers by claim type; sufficiency_threshold: BP.3 defines source-governance architecture without populating or validating real evidence; evidence_rationale: BP.3 controls how evidence may be used across BP.1–BP.11; cannot_support: demand, adoption, PMF, compliance, feasibility, commercial readiness, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: source inventory, source classifications, and claim-support map are not populated. Support: governed source register and evidence map. Revise: evidence ladder, source library, or source-use rules change. Invalidate: sources cannot be traced or use boundaries cannot be enforced.
nodes.linked_uncertainties: BP.12 candidate — source-governance gap; BP.12 candidate — source-misuse risk
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat source existence, citation, or classification as claim validation. Must not infer demand, WTP, procurement readiness, PMF, compliance, feasibility, commercial readiness, or investor readiness from weak or misused sources.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if new source rules, evidence tiers, source conflicts, unsupported claims, or source-misuse risks are identified.
nodes.notes_limitations: BP.3 governs evidence use; it does not validate business claims.

nodes.purpose: Defines how candidate sources are identified, logged, and made reviewable.
nodes.required_output: Source inventory; source metadata; source status; inclusion/exclusion notes.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: internal_architecture, uploaded sources, Source Library where available; evidence_tier_required: E1 for architecture; sufficiency_threshold: inventory fields are defined but not populated as validated evidence; evidence_rationale: source audit governs evidence handling before claim support; cannot_support: claim validation, demand, PMF, compliance, feasibility, commercial readiness, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: source inventory not populated. Support: uploaded or approved sources logged. Revise: source fields or source scope changes. Invalidate: source inventory cannot trace source origin.
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat listed sources as sufficient evidence merely because they are inventoried.
nodes.reopen_condition: Reopen if new source families, source rules, or evidence standards are introduced.
nodes.notes_limitations: Architecture only; does not validate any claim.

nodes.purpose: Identify all candidate sources that may be used to support BP claims.
nodes.required_output: Source identification register listing each candidate source by name, type, and origin.
nodes.evidence_requirement: source_family_required: internal_architecture, Source Library; evidence_tier_required: E1; sufficiency_threshold: each candidate source is uniquely identified and traceable; evidence_rationale: identification is prerequisite to classification and use; cannot_support: claim validation, demand, PMF, or investor readiness.
nodes.evidence_gaps_assumptions: Gap: source list not compiled. Support: uploaded or referenced sources. Revise: new sources added. Invalidate: sources cannot be identified.
nodes.prohibited_claims_inference_patterns: Must not treat source identification as source validation.
